rows.text: Almost there, Saber. Up ahead is the Dreamscape Fast Food Restaurant.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: A restaurant in an unknown world... I wonder what kind of delicious surprises await...
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Hmm? Isn't that Robin? What's she doing here?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Oh, you've got the wrong idea... I may have taken some history electives back at Paperfold University, but I'm hardly the right person for scientific research.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Sorry for just showing up out of the blue. The Astral Express's trailblazing journey is always a whirlwind, so I try not to disrupt your plans.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I'm here today on someone's behalf, to bring you a gift.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Haha, not surprising at all. This so-called "Holy Grail" Curio is bizarre indeed.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I knew you wouldn't forget. Even in a dreamland like Penacony, that was a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: The Ho... Holy Grail War!?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Old Oti gave me this "Holy Grail" as a token of gratitude for everyone who participated in the war. I wanted to display it on the Radiant Feldspar. He agreed wholeheartedly, saying...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Because every shining palace has its forgotten corners, gathering dust, ignored. And in those places, there are people with countless, unfulfilled wishes. That's why the Grail would come here.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Good. I'll make sure to repay you with a glorious victory.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: No way! A knight would never stoop to that!
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Oh, please! This is Dreamflux Reef, and news spreads like wildfire in this place.
rows.speaker: Jessie

rows.text: Haha, trying to stay low-key, huh? Don't worry, I won't sell you out.
rows.speaker: Jessie

rows.text: And this must be the Heroic Spirit you summoned, huh? Dare I ask, Miss, which famous person from Penaconian history do you represent?
rows.speaker: Jessie

rows.text: The lady next to me needs to replenish some energy.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Then make it fifty. The lady next to me needs to replenish some energy.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Wow, you looked so serious and reliable, and yet you're now telling bad jokes!
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: With so many Halovian Winged Burgers, it'll take a little time to prepare. Please be patient, folks!
rows.speaker: Jessie

rows.text: Sorry to interrupt, dear guests, but... if you're gonna fight, maybe you should eat first? Your Halovian Winged Burgers are ready!
rows.speaker: Jessie

rows.text: No problem at all. I love seeing people smile after they're full. But your Servant's appetite is truly impressive!
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: No, no... We must unite everyone, temporarily setting aside any fighting.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: It's about making peace... not begging. At the very least, we should show them we have no intention of fighting.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: That's right, exactly.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: From what I know of Old Oti, he won't stop this game no matter what.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: But for now, I'll follow your lead. However, if the situation changes when trying to form alliances with other Servants, I'll make my own decisions.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Huh? You've already figured out how to automatically translate his swearing in your head?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Putting the content aside, Boothill isn't exactly good at typing, let alone this kind of formal letter format...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Looks like... the "mutual slaughter" has already begun.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Count me in too.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Don't worry, Master. No matter what happens, I'll protect you.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: I believe he'll make it out safely too. Either way, this is a good opportunity to ally with him and stop the fighting.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: The enemy has set up a trap. If we pull back now, we avoid the risk. But losing two allies would put us at an even greater disadvantage in later attacks.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: It's been a while, [Trailblazer]. Mr. Screwllum said you'd stop by today, so I figured I'd wait here for a bit.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: So this is the device for testing the "Divergent Universe," huh?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: You're interested in the Divergent Universe too?
Why didn't you leave me a message?
Do you still remember the Holy Grail War we had back in Penacony?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Not a clue.
Even though I still recall that adventure we went through together, some of the details get a bit hazy when I think back on it.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: You bet I do!
However, every time I think back to our adventure, some details get a bit hazy. That so-called "Holy Grail" is such a bizarre Curio.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: It's indeed bizarre. This so-called "Holy Grail" Curio... Even though I still recall what we went through together, some of the details always get a bit hazy when I think back on it.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: "Hohohoho! What better decoration for the Radiant Feldspar than a cup said to grant any wish? Talk about grandeur!"
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Mr. Screwllum was entrusted to neutralize the power of the "Holy Grail." Now it's just an ordinary dream bubble, stripped of its wish-granting properties.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I've always wondered: If the Grail really could grant you a wish, what would yours be?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: (A wish, huh... Feels like someone asked me a similar question during the Holy Grail War...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Your thoughts gradually rewind to the beginning of that Holy Grail War as many vague details gain clarity.
It was a long time ago... or not so long ago...
I've always been a gambler, teetering between bad luck and incredible fortune. But even for me, this draw of the cards is a bit...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Still, I have to say, I kinda like your Servant. A partner who plays by the rules and knows his boundaries? I'd take that over you schemers any day. At least he's trustworthy.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: No doubt, he's an incredible Servant. But...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Who exactly are you in Penaconian history?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Master, do I look like I have any ties to this bizarre world of yours?
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Looks like, just like your Servant, he's from another world.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: That's actually a relief. At least this nightmare of indulgence and debauchery isn't my world's future.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Forkin' hell. So two outsiders summoned two more outsiders? The Holy Grail War allergic to local talent now or somethin'?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Make that three. There are three Servants from another world here.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Oh! Cú Chulainn! Things didn't go your way, huh?
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Did you just say my True Name out loud? Ever heard of tact?
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: What's the big deal? No one here knows us. No one's ever heard of {RUBY_B#Ireland}Erin{RUBY_E#}, or the Hound of Culann.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: But that also means we're at a huge disadvantage. We're fighting against Heroic Spirits who get buffed by this world's power.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Man, all I asked you to do was a little recon. How'd you end up looking this beat?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Don't even start. I almost got two Masters in one sweep, but then Assassin covered his Master's escape, and the other one... that gray-haired kid summoned—
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Fork! Gray hair!? That's one of ours! Why the heck were you fighting {M#him?}{F#her?}
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: You're the one who told me to go after the most annoying targets!
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Ugh... Guess we'll have to clear up that little misunderstanding when we meet — Huh? You said {M#his}{F#her} Heroic Spirit is like you guys?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: That's right, Master. Their Servant is...
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: A Saber we're very familiar with.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Her? Well, that is an unexpected reunion.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Are you guys often summoned into worlds that aren't your own?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: "Aren't our own"? Most of the time, we're in situations that are foreign to us: someone else's era, nation, war.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: But I've never seen a world so completely alien before.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: That said, as a Counter Guardian — you don't need to know what that means — my job is to show up when a Holy Grail War goes wrong. Maybe the other two were pulled here for the same reason.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Ah, I see. So it's your fault we're all stuck here.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: What do you mean by a "wrong" Holy Grail War? Do you mean that, in your world, the Holy Grail War is a common ritual, but in our world, Old Oti completely botched the process?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: It's not exactly normal in our world, either. But you guys definitely screwed it up. First off, the Grail is not a toy. And it surely isn't something amateur mages like you should be messing with.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: And this time, our physical bodies weren't even constructed from magical energy.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: If I had to guess, the so-called "Grail" must have tapped into something similar to magecraft to create this pseudo Holy Grail War.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: A corrupted ritual... a Holy Grail in the hands of someone who is the host of this war. Lancer, do you want me to spell it out?
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Might as well slap "Mastermind" on their forehead. Well, at least my Master this time doesn't seem like the kind of idiot who'd abuse their Command Spells...
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: That makes things simple. We just find the muddle-fudger behind this Holy Grail War and drag them out into the open.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: But what if they're waiting for us to come knocking, so they can wipe us all out in one go?
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Ugh, it's annoying but unavoidable. I believe I'm the only one here with formal training in magecraft. I'll try and analyze our enemy's setup, see if I can figure out their real goal.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: As for you guys... whether you hide or attack head-on, you should be safe for now.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: A breeze blows past and the blue-haired man disappears.
[Trailblazer]'s texting me now? What the fork? These lines... Did {F#s}he just get possessed by the Knight of Beauty? Whatever. Not the first time {F#s}he's acted like this.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: What, already hitting you up for revenge?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: No. {M#He}{F#She} wants us to meet at Clock Studios Theme Park. Says {F#s}he wants to talk about an alliance.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: In the meantime, at Dreamflux Reef.
I thought a Heroic Spirit would look... I don't know, more special?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: This isn't quite my true form. But I'm afraid this is the only way I can appear before you.
Summoned at your request, I am... Caster.
I would, of course, prefer to be honest with you. But every time I try to say my own True Name, it turns into this — ███, ███, ███.
rows.speaker: Caster

rows.text: Dissonance... But that's your name.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: It was. But it's been trademarked. Copyrighted. Owned by someone else. I'm sorry, Master.
rows.speaker: Caster

rows.text: Just call me Robin. I'm not used to being called anything else.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Miss Robin, I'm sorry if this isn't what you were hoping for. I'm just a faded star from the Age of Dreaming, a piece of dead skin in an industry that sheds its past without a second thought.
rows.speaker: Caster

rows.text: I was brilliant, once. Who was I? Well... maybe you'd find the answer buried in some old, forgotten magazine. They used to call me the Eternal Silver-Screen Beauty, the Golden Note of Xipe's Legacy...
rows.speaker: Caster

rows.text: I've had even more names. But ever since I first stepped into the limelight, I've never had my own.
rows.speaker: Caster

rows.text: Not even in death. Not even now, when I've been dragged from the grave to perform on this new world's old stage. Every time I even try to speak my name, it gets drowned out by that cursed dissonance—
rows.speaker: Caster

rows.text: But it's my name! My name! Mine!
rows.speaker: Caster

rows.text: I'm sorry...
rows.speaker: Caster

rows.text: It's okay. Let it out. I get it. Sometimes I want to lose control, too. When we're on stage, under the spotlight, performers like us have to keep our composure.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Since you can't use your real name... what should I call you?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Caster. That's the title the Grail assigned me.
rows.speaker: Caster

rows.text: No. I don't like that. I want a name you chose, not a name that was chosen for you.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Thank you, Miss Robin. Then call me Miss Note. For now.
rows.speaker: Caster

rows.text: Funny... I don't remember being this emotional when I was alive. Maybe my fractured Spirit Origin is affecting my personality.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: No True Name. No Noble Phantasm. Just this ridiculous talent for theatrics. But I'll do what I can, however little that may be. I'll fight for you and myself to earn a chance to wish upon the Holy Grail.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: You want to win? To me, the only real victory is making this war disappear.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: And that's something weapons can never achieve. Only song can do that.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: But people always remember the ones who win wars. Never the ones who try to end them...
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Whether you want to end this war or win it, you're going to need allies. No performance is complete with only the lead on stage.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: I know. I was just thinking the same thing. Out of everyone in this war, there are at least two people I can trust. I've already invited one of them, and I plan to lay everything on the table for {M#him.}{F#her.}
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Penacony... Cityscapes floating in the sky like clouds, where ice cream and cotton candy just chirp and jump straight into your mouth... This is incredible.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Just like you said, Master. This world is steeped in dreams.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: But it wasn't until we arrived at this place, Dreamflux Reef, that I truly understood why the Holy Grail chose this world.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Why?
This land proves Penacony isn't a dream kingdom, but an exaggerated reflection of reality.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Alright, enough about that. Let's find something to eat. Listening to your stomach rumble is making me hungry too.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Uh... Servants don't bring money when they materialize in the world. Is your wallet... good to go?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: No worries. The fast food joints in Dreamflux Reef are cheap with big portions.
Then I'm relieved. As a Servant who is a veteran of many battles, I don't really care about the quality of food.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Don't sweat it, I've got plenty of cash!
Well, if we run fast enough, it's free.
If it really comes to that, I'll just have to work as a server to pay it off.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: My dear guests, welcome! What would you like to eat?
rows.speaker: Jessie

rows.text: Wait a minute... isn't that our Festive Superstar? You're here for that... Holy Grail War, right?
rows.speaker: Jessie

rows.text: You guys know all the gossip around here too?
I'm not—! I'm not involved!
Sorry, but in the Holy Grail War, revealing my True Name would be a major breach of security.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Gotcha, gotcha. Like a secret recipe, huh?
rows.speaker: Jessie

rows.text: Why don't you tell me this instead? What's the best dish on the menu?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: If this is your first time in Dreamflux Reef, I highly recommend the Halovian Winged Burger. It's a burger you won't find anywhere else.
rows.speaker: Jessie

rows.text: Our store only uses pure organic ingredients sourced from the Memory Zone's farms. The soil they're cultivated in is free of harmful emotions...
rows.speaker: Jessie

rows.text: Thank you, but no need to explain. We'll go with the Halovian Winged Burger.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Alright, we'd like 100 burgers!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Okay... wait, did you say a hundred? Are you sure about that?
rows.speaker: Jessie

rows.text: Just in case some of them fly away.
Is this... a text from Mr. Boothill?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: For the love of Akivili, he's cursing up a storm!
Wait, wait, this absolutely isn't from him!
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: This isn't from him at all, is it?
See, peace is just the interlude in a war. That Boothill... he's probably already been taken down.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: No, he's a seasoned warrior. There's no way he's out this early. But someone must've gotten their hands on his phone and is using his identity to lure us to Clock Studios Theme Park.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: This invitation is written so earnestly. I guess we'll have to graciously accept.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Yeah, I was thinking the same. If we rush over now, there's still a chance to save Mr. Boothill. What do you all think?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I like diving right into the trap.
To be honest, I'm a bit on edge.
Boothill will be fine!
Then let's head out!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: So, Saber... what wish would you make to the Holy Grail?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: If I'm lucky enough to win, I hope...
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Hold on, let's talk later, Master. I sense another Servant approaching.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Two Halovian Winged Burgers, two bottles of Sousa Juice. Miss Note, is that okay?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Of course... but I'm afraid this isn't exactly a quiet spot to dine. We have a rather... noticeable Servant in front of us.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: It's been a while, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Miss Note, this is the trustworthy friend I mentioned to you earlier.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Oh... they're a friend of yours, Master?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: It's a {RUBY_B#False Holy Grail War}mockery of a war{RUBY_E#}, but you set it up so intricately... I don't get it.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: The Twelve Hours that referenced the passage of time, and this {RUBY_B#Grand Theater}"moon"{RUBY_E#} placed right at the heart of it all.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Anyone with magecraft training can feel power continuously flowing into this place, but this world has no "magecraft" or "mages."
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: So, did you really design this whole Holy Grail War, old man? You don't exactly look like a mage.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Ohohoho! The sharp instincts of a businessman are enough for me to know where and when to make my moves, and the Holy Grail has told me everything I need to know.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: You are the Servant of that Galaxy Ranger... I didn't think your nose would be even sharper than the Bloodhound Family's minions.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Is it really wise for you to charge in here on your own instead of loyally staying at your Master's side? That cowboy's in quite a pinch right now and would appreciate a speedy rescue...
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: What a pain. If I blow your head off right here, that'd save my metal clump of a Master too, no?
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Let me offer you some advice from experience — the Holy Grail never grants wishes the way people expect. All it leaves behind are dead souls buried by their desires.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Ohohoho! I appreciate the advice, truly. In that case, am I not giving the Holy Grail a new purpose? It'll become an entertainment spectacle much more worthy of investment than some wish-granting chalice.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Heh, "entertainment spectacle"... I get it now. That clicks pretty well with the essence of the Holy Grail. No wonder it managed to power this Holy Grail War.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: You recount the fantastical dream you had during Penacony's Charmony Festival to Saber, how a man dreamed of creating a paradise kingdom with his own power.

Once, a king offered themself upon the altar — a lone sacrifice in exchange for a dream of Paradise on Earth. How eerily similar it all feels... to what unfolded during the Charmony Festival in Penacony.
I've been wondering what you could possibly put into the Holy Grail apart from wine, given this is a barren world where Mystics have completely degraded.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: But if something could replace magical energy, and manage to infuse the Holy Grail with enough power to create miracles... well, that changes things entirely.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Instead of something that must maintain the Concealment of Mystics, the Holy Grail War will become a public entertainment spectacle instead.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Then, the people on this dream-soaked planet will come to believe in the miracle of the Holy Grail through learning its rituals and witnessing the summoning of Heroic Spirits.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: And so, little by little, their wishes will turn into fuel, coating the Holy Grail in a fabricated miracle — and the farce you've orchestrated will end up stomping all over those wishes!
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Quite the impressive insight, Servant from another world. Your presence here was certainly a surprise to me, but you and your friends are needed. The Holy Grail needs more efficient fuel — and that means... you.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Where did she send us?
Miss Note... No, ████. It's time for you to show Penacony your true charm.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: I did what you wanted me to do...
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Well done, my old friend. So many years have passed, but I still remember every performance you gave, every dance you danced, every melody you sang...
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: You were like a blooming iris, but I prefer how you are now compared to your heydays on the stage... stripped of all the external pretenses, so simple, so ordinary.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Enough, Oti. Outdated metaphors are as revolting as last night's leftovers. I've kept my promise. Now it's your turn.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: There's no rush, my old friend. Everything you desire can be obtained without magecraft or miracles — money is all it takes. The so-called Holy Grail is nothing more than a vessel crafted from gold.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: And the real stars of this show are about to make their entrance. Your job is to hold them off until the last step of the ritual is complete. Once that is done, I will honor my end of the deal.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Oti, looks like your business acumen has rotted along with this world.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: I could barely restrain that one Servant, and now you expect me to take them all on?
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: There, beneath a tree, a tiny knight doll rested, as if lost in a dream that would never end.
Ohohoho! Don't be so modest. Unlike Grady, you're a true artist! You had the talent to bring thousands of characters to life all on your own. You are the perfect counter to these "heroes."
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: It looks a bit like you.
I will give you the power the Holy Grail has accumulated so you can crush them all. Then, this grand spectacle will come to a glorious finale!
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Fork it, wasn't that blue guy supposed to scout this place ahead of us? Haven't even heard a single peep from him so far... Could that old man have pulled a fast one on him?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: No signs of battle. This doesn't quite seem like something Lancer would do.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: From what I know about that man, he might even stir up some pointless fights, just to walk away happy...
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Miss Note! I'm glad you're okay—
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Wait. Something's off. Miss Note, I trust that you've seen Lancer here, haven't you?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Yes. He came to the Grand Theater with his spear raised and ready, eager to impale Old Oti on the curtain. I couldn't agree more with his approach...
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: But I still have dreams left unfulfilled in this miraculous second life... So, I asked him to take a break.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: And I must insist that every one of you take a break as well... until Mr. Oti finishes the ritual.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Fear not. There will be no pain. Please leave your passion and ambitions on the stage, like how actors shed their fatigue and makeup behind the curtains... and rest.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Where's this...?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: So was Britain saved?
How... is this possible...? Why am I in Britain?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Yes. I remember it all... every tree, every blade of grass, the fields, the wind's scent, and this town... Does Caster think she can trap me with these memories?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Hmph. This town is nothing less than where my life as a knight began.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Oh! Artorius! Here to draw the sword, aren't you?
rows.speaker: Young Village Neighbor

rows.text: You're calling me Artorius...? Is it Aiden?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: I knew it. That mage Merlin spun such a tall tale, something about "Whosoe'er pulleth out this sword of this stone is rightwise king of all England." Even an apprentice knight wouldn't be able to resist that.
rows.speaker: Young Village Neighbor

rows.text: That being said... A little fellow like you drawing the sword and becoming king? I really can't picture that.
rows.speaker: Young Village Neighbor

rows.text: You remind me of Sunday...
...Right. I agree. I hope the Sword in the Stone manages to pick the right king.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: The only thing that can grant your wish would be the Holy Grail...
Master. Let's go.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: What did he just call you...?
Artorius. That is the male name I used. After all, a female king would have had a very difficult time ruling Britain back in those days.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: We've returned to the moment right before I drew the sword from the stone.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: ...I thought Caster would use monsters, foreign armies, or even dragons to trap us here.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: ...How I miss all this. I never returned here after I left as a knight. What we see before us is the childish dream I had when I was still just a nameless nobody.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: ...What a shame. She's created such a fantasy for me, yet I don't even have a mount.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: My greatest dream as a child was to have a mount of my own. To become a knight. To ride a horse. To follow this very path across the fields and reach the grasslands where Ector's house lies.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: He's the old knight tasked with raising me... he was my "father" in a sense.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: You called out, your voice echoing, but the drawn-out words never reached the Servant. In the moment she hesitated, fate had already been sealed—
In truth... you were never here at all. What remains in this place is merely a shadow of you who fell into a Noble Phantasm, lingering in the dream of another.
He always wore a stern expression but laughed at the smallest things... He always told me that he hoped I'd become the "ideal king" for this land.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: But... in the end, he never got to see me become a king...
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: I'm sorry, Master. I got carried away talking about my past. Now that we're here, how about we set aside our worries about illusions and dreams, and I'll show you around my hometown instead?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: If this is the soldier summoned by Caster, they must be an incredibly powerful opponent.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Now —

I've never seen a toy like this. My first fifteen years were mostly spent caring for horses and honing my swordsmanship. During my breaks, a mage named Merlin would visit me in my dreams, and teach me about ruling as a king.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: What about you, Master? How did you spend your childhood? You've never talked about your past.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: The girl seemed drawn by something. Her gaze wandered to the end of the path.
Actually, I never went to school...
I... don't remember a lot about my past...
Really? But you sound more knowledgeable than the bards of Camelot when you talk about all the news from the outside world.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Humanity has entered the age of the stars. Wisdom that was once unimaginably arcane has now become common knowledge...
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: The only thing I remember is being woken up by someone in a space station.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Really? ...No wonder your personality is so carefree. Is it because you don't have a past holding you back, Master?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: My earliest memory was boarding a train headed for the stars and meeting many kindred spirits as friends. Though I have no past, I have a future.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I'm really lucky.
I'm totally free.
I became the person I wanted to be.
I'm really lucky.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I'm totally free.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I became the person I wanted to be.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Well... Even in the face of hardship, you are still continuing on your wonderful journey. I wish I did that in my life.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Once upon a time, I also wanted to become a specific person. I wanted to save the land I stood on and the people who lived upon it. I wanted to repel the tyranny of King Vortigern the White Dragon. I wanted to deliver my people from the foreign invaders' hostile rule.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: I wanted to be the ideal king my people dreamed of, someone who would save Britain. For that... I would have sacrificed everything.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: The mage told me that if I could pull the sword from the stone, then I would achieve my wish. Everyone thought that I would save Britain.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: I didn't save Britain.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: I once believed that once I slew Vortigern, expelled the foreign invaders, gathered the Knights of the Round Table, and built the impenetrable castle of Camelot, peace would finally come to Britain.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: But that was all a fleeting dream. The knights who once served me abandoned me, and some even raised armies to challenge my rule... Britain was once again engulfed in war.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Merlin had already warned me of all this before I drew the Sword of Selection...
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: He told me that once I drew the sword, I would meet a tragic end, hated by all.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: And while the kingdom was in its prime, he also told me...
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: That Britain would one day fall, and its current prosperity was built on the suffering of its king.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Yet I thought... I could carry the weight of the kingdom's pain and trade it for the peace of the people, the sacrifice would be worth it, and I would be willing to face my thankless end.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Miss Robin's older brother? His thoughts and actions sound a lot similar to mine.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: I promised everyone that I would build the ideal kingdom, but I left the land of Britain with endless wars, dying warriors, and starving children.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: The one who deserves to face destruction is me, not my country or my people. That's how it should have been.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: So this is the Sword in the Stone...?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: The man looks at you with exasperation written all over his face, visibly biting back a snarky remark.
You try to yell at the researcher before you, but your wavering voice gives a different response.
I've wondered countless times... had I not drawn this sword, or had there been someone more suited to be king...
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Would Britain have truly become the utopia I dreamed of? And what kind of a life would I have lived?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: To pull out the sword and become king, or to give up and stay in my homeland to quietly live out my days.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: But, was that answer truly what you thought? Or was it some sort of illusive manipulation? You try to piece together what has happened, but your memories feel more distant with every passing second.
She's brought me back to the moment I made my choice...
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Saber, do you... wish to stay?
Master... I'm so... tired.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: I wish I had a horse... to ride across these fields before the sun sets...
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: You're on the verge of shouting, but just then, a sliver of doubt creeps inside you.
The bat you always have at your side... is no longer there. Then again, did you ever really have it in the first place?
But where would you go? Is there anywhere you can go? You're young, with no special talents. Isn't your best bet a cushy job with full benefits, clocking in every day until the world ends?
Saber—!
Yes. That's it. Calmly and nicely, drop the fight. By now, the job feels like second nature. Might as well tidy up the last of the files.
You glance at his work tag. On it, just a single letter — A. Department: Domestic Services. Wait... since when does the space station have a Domestic Services Department?
She was nothing more than an ordinary girl. Playing the part of a king was already painful enough. Why should we force her to continue in the delusion known as Heroic Spirits?
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Better to cast aside her sword, abandon her glory, and become a nameless nobody who watches the world's grand show on the sidelines.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: I'll help all of you to remove the hero's garish makeup bit by bit, until I've wiped away even the choice you've made to become a hero, until I've wiped away all the pain you've endured on this thorny road.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: I've prepared a simple and happy life for all of you in this show — Including you, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: So, newcomer, are you staying?
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: Someone like you has probably already burned through all your luck just trying to get into the Herta Space Station, but I'll go through the motions and confirm it anyway.
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: Just so you know, working at the Department of Cosmic Geography isn't as easy as you think.
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: Who? Madam Herta? Well, this IS her space station.
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: Sorry, there are no conference rooms available at your requested time.
Sorry, there are no conference rooms available at your requested time.
Sorry, there are no conference rooms available at your requested time.

Something stirs in your memory, sparks from an engine streaking past the space station, the faint weightlessness before the Express conducts a warp jump... Wait, no. None of that is real. Researcher, you should be focusing on your task at hand.
Alright. Including the two new system-generated meetings, just 897 more to go, and the list is done.
That's right, exactly.
You're in the zone now, handling the work before you with practiced ease.
You ever tried fishing, {M#buddy?}{F#lass?} Don't be fooled by the vacuum outside. There's still plenty to catch.
rows.speaker: Mysterious Researcher L

rows.text: Hmph. Look. I thought I was pretty impressive too when I first arrived.
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: Oh, I see... If things are tough, you could always talk to Asta. She's sure to help you out.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Oh, I see... If things are tough, you could always talk to Asta. She's sure to help you out.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But you'll be beaten into shape in no time. You're just a regular researcher on this station. No one's gonna even bat an eye at your so-called talents and smarts.
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: But I'm the Galactic Baseballer!
But I defeated Tatalov.
Himeko frowns, as if your question has caught her off guard. An unsettling sensation flickers through your mind. You've never boarded the Express. So who is this... "Pom-Pom" you speak of?
But I'm a Nameless! I don't belong here!
Is that really how you feel? If joining the Astral Express doesn't change your life for the better... What then?
Still thinking about the Astral Express? You've been wrestling with that choice for ages, and still haven't made up your mind.
If you board the Express, what waits for you may be nothing but danger and the terrifying unknown. Your deeds will be forgotten in time, and your journey will eventually come to an end.
So you are glad you stayed. No ticket. No bat. No danger. Just a quiet, peaceful, and undisturbed life.
And? I'm the Cosmic Geographer.
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: Who's that? A game character?
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: ... Are you dreaming or something? Maybe you should take a sick day and get a check-up at the Medical Department.
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: I'm a bit of a fan of the Astral Express, and I know that every Nameless who boards it has been through some incredible adventures. So, tell me. What great deeds have you done?
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: I need to set off!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Oh, I've heard of that! Apparently, a valuable relic was stolen from the space station. It was swallowed by a mysterious intruder, which then led to an attack from the Antimatter Legion.
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: If it weren't for Madam Herta stepping in to handle the crisis, we'd all be burnt to a crisp by now. Any idea who that mysterious intruder was?
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: You mean the Lord Ravager who recently appeared on the Xianzhou and caused a huge ruckus?
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: From what I've heard, her plan was foiled by the General of the Luofu... but the Xianzhou people paid a heavy price for it. Listen, don't use someone else's tragedy as your bragging material.
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: Let me guess, next you'll say you were invited to the Charmony Festival? And became the Festive Superstar?
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: Where did she send me???
Look at me in the eyes and say that again.

Haha. Oh, I know what's happening now! The Department of Implement Arts imported a batch of dream bubbles. Loads of young naïve researchers have been wasting entire days in them, ignoring even their paid work.
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: You probably ate too much of that memoria too and thought those illusions were real. Why else would you believe you're a Nameless aboard the Express?
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: Well... I can't say I blame you. I heard the Express did invite you to join them, but you turned them down. Are you regretting that choice now?
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: But I DID board the Express!
I became afraid.
I facetanked the Doomsday Beast's Ultimate!
I don't know.
Yep, you guessed it. It was you, {M#brat}{F#lass}. The only reason you got a job here is that Lead Researcher Asta took pity on you.
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: I defeated Phantylia on the Xianzhou!
Yes, I regret my choice.
I woke Penacony from its eternal slumber!
I... I don't know what to say...
I became... afraid.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I... don't know...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I... regret my choice.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Well, your resume doesn't show any particular skills, so I'll start you off with some light tasks...
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: Sort the Department of Cosmic Geography's expenditure report from the past six months. Schedule research meetings for the upcoming month. Collect project proposals from all levels of researchers. Yeah, that should keep you busy for a while.
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: Am I really a researcher?
About the Astral Express and the Nameless. Like sand under the waves, your memories crumble and fade. And suddenly, you understand — why Saber chose to stay, even just for a moment.

Why didn't you step aboard the Astral Express back then, on that split-second impulse? It no longer matters. The researcher in the Department of Cosmic Geography standing before you watches you closely, perhaps searching for words of comfort, or maybe looking for the right joke to shatter the heavy silence. Eventually, he speaks.
Isn't this the Department of Cosmic Geography?
What else would you be? Madam Herta?
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: Don't be so surprised. Our department is at the bottom of the food chain on the station... this work happens all the time.
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: I'm off, [Trailblazer]. Be sure to do your job well.
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: He turns to leave... yet could not help himself from looking back at you.

Yeah, sometimes I regret picking the Geography of the Universe course when I was fourteen and walking away from Quantum History... I felt math was just too tough for me back then. But now, I ask myself... Would I still be stuck in this dead-end job if I made a different choice?
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: No no no. C'mon. Don't worry about the what-ifs. Why waste time regretting a choice you've already made? Look at me, things aren't so bad here, are they?
rows.speaker: Lv. 4 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: This is all wrong! You scream internally, but the fury is fleeting.
You're late, newcomer. A few more system days of delay and we'll miss the reimbursement deadline.
rows.speaker: Lv. 3 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: I'll cut you some slack given that you're new. Now get to work.
rows.speaker: Lv. 3 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: (What a messy desk. Am I supposed to organize all this stuff? Where do I even start?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Sort by budget category.
Don't push your luck.
Is this really what you want? Take a breath. Don't lash out. Focus on what you truly need to do.
Take out the baseball bat and give her a good beating.
I quit.
Complete the basic tasks.
Sort by budget category.
You're too slow. Keep going like this and you'll still be here when the Amber Lord makes THEIR next hammer swing.
rows.speaker: Lv. 3 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: But I really feel like we've...
What are you standing around for? You think space bionic snails are going to do the work for you?
rows.speaker: Lv. 3 Geography Dept. Researcher

rows.text: I dreamt that I was part of the Holy Grail War.
(These reports are endless... and the stuff written in there is really weird.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Hold on. I think I've seen that person over there before.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: If you're going to ask me "Have we met before," my answer is gonna be "no."
C'mon, Uncle A, don't you ever feel like you don't belong here?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I get it. I really do. Dozens of researchers come up to me every day, all claiming they don't belong here.
rows.speaker: Mysterious Researcher A

rows.text: You glance at him, wanting to say something, but decided not to.
They think they should be somewhere else because life isn't going their way. It's just another dressed-up excuse to escape reality.
rows.speaker: Mysterious Researcher A

rows.text: Days pass. After long hours of sorting, you're finally done with the work.
Although an uncanny feeling lingers in your chest, before it's resolved, you should take a break.
Drifting quietly over the surface of a dream, suspended in the moment before you sink.
As long as your instinct is just to back down and run, you'll run out of places to go even if you manage to get out of this place.
rows.speaker: Mysterious Researcher A

rows.text: Personally? I think this place isn't so bad. No world-threatening crises, no freaks trying to end humanity. The kitchen's convenient, too... though the ingredients are a bit odd.
rows.speaker: Mysterious Researcher A

rows.text: We've still got a little girl who throws around gemstones like dirt, but it's pretty much a utopia for most people.
rows.speaker: Mysterious Researcher A

rows.text: There's no turning back once you leave your ordinary life behind.
rows.speaker: Mysterious Researcher A

rows.text: Changed your mind, huh? I knew it. You don't really want to leave, do you?
rows.speaker: Mysterious Researcher A

rows.text: (I'm exhausted... I feel like I can't even think anymore.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (But deep down? I still feel like I don't belong here.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Let me tell you a story about a king... a king named Uther.
He ruled the people of Britain before I showed up. And after my appearance, he launched an attack against the White Dragon to protect his people, a battle that ended in defeat.
Even so, people still called him the greatest king. What do you think made him a hero?
The innate glory of being a king.
The deeds he achieved as a knight.
The courage he exhibited as a human.
Great. Couldn't be better.
Not so well.
It's been... really bad.
No. The names of kings from other tribes, kings equal to his stature, have all been forgotten.
No. There were knights more courageous than him by his side, but their names didn't survive in time.
He raised his sword to challenge a dragon he knew he could never defeat. The sword shattered, the bow snapped, and he was beheaded. As a human, everything about him was destined to fail...
But the way he raised his sword to bring deliverance left a shining star in Britain's darkest nights.
The stars we see may not be their original forms, but their light isn't a lie. It will shine for ages, lighting the way for the next hero.
That {RUBY_B#Miss Note}Heroic Spirit who lost her name{RUBY_E#} referred to our lives as "a stage," and she used her Noble Phantasm to erase the star's radiance.
But Master... if you still have courage... if you're still willing to become that star, then all the spectators who have seen you will also step onto the stage, becoming heroes themselves.
Any new passengers aboard?
Look at me. Talking big all of a sudden and doing a bad imitation of Merlin.
Where are you?
I'm waiting for someone who's about to take the stage. I'm also riding through the wilderness. The dream is nearing its end, Master, for me and you.
(What a strange dream... I should get to work.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: What if what awaits you isn't a grand adventure, but endless cleaning, constant repairs, wounds that never heal, and death steeped in despair... What will you do then?
What if you can't help anyone? What if you become a dead weight on the Express? What if a Nameless gives their life to save you, yet everyone silently wishes you'd just leave... What will you do?
Think about it. What answer should you give?
(Scheduling Department of Cosmic Geography meetings for the next month... this should be easier than yesterday, right?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Hahaha, then I guess I'm the model fisherman.
rows.speaker: Mysterious Researcher L

rows.text: The chief is too busy chasing those Ruan Mei Creations that ran away. He won't have time to read your report.
rows.speaker: Mysterious Researcher L

rows.text: Well, no worries. You work here, and I'll slack off. We each get what we need.
rows.speaker: Mysterious Researcher L

rows.text: So you'll finally admit...
The voices that once spoke to you fell silent in an instant. They never spoke again.
A bat — plain, unimpressive, yet strangely familiar.
You once believed you'd never hold it again in this lifetime.
(The Astral Express... I turned down their invitation back then...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Did I really make the right choice?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Long time no see, [Trailblazer]. How's life been on the space station?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I'm glad to see you've settled in here.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: We traveled to many places after we parted ways: Belobog, the Xianzhou Luofu, Penacony... There were both good and bad moments along the way.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: How's Pom-Pom?
How's Dan Heng doing?
How's Mr. Yang?
At the same time, the host of the Holy Grail War is sitting elsewhere watching the advert with interest...
Terrific! I loved how you used the word "survivor" instead of "victor" to rally the contestants. Nothing stirs up a person's drive quite like the goal of simply staying alive.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: What an inspiring speech, Mr. Oti. Even {RUBY_B#Founder of the IPC}Louis Fleming{RUBY_E#} himself couldn't have done it better!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Hohoho! Easy on the sweet talk, kid. I'm not here for your flattery. I brought you in because I expect you to give it your all... and become the "survivor."
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Mr. Oti, summoning a Servant this early... Isn't that a little against the rules?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Hahaha! I didn't realize our producer cared so much about the rules!
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: You bet I care about the rules! It's fun to break them in the heat of the moment, but if trouble comes knocking afterward, we're the ones who get hurt!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Hohoho... Rest assured. For this Holy Grail War, I have the final say on all the rules.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Producer, time's ticking. Let's hurry and check out the other participants!
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Whoa! Looks like our honorary member is dodging the question! Could it be they've got a secret wish they don't want anyone to know?
rows.speaker: Reporter

rows.text: Well then, do you think you've got what it takes to win the Holy Grail War?
rows.speaker: Reporter

rows.text: Ooh! Dodging the question again, huh? Must be hiding a mace up their sleeve!
rows.speaker: Reporter

rows.text: Right, right. So, honorary member, which legendary figure from history are you planning to summon? Don't tell me you're as clueless about Penacony's history as I am?
rows.speaker: Reporter

rows.text: Oh, c'mon, {M#buddy}{F#girl}, it's a rare treat for us Belobogian folks to travel off-world. Running into an old friend on an alien planet? That's pure joy. Sure, the occasion might be a little weird, but don't tell me you don't recognize us?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: As Penacony's last Festive Superstar, [Trailblazer] was once the center of everyone's attention.
And now, with the unprecedented First Penaconian Holy Grail War about to kick off, [Trailblazer] is back in the spotlight!
Come on, {M#buddy}{F#girl}, show the audience that... uh... what's it called... tattoo... on your hand?
It's the Command Spells!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Right! Command Spells! Proof of your selection to join the Holy Grail War. They say its power lets you command legendary figures from Penacony's history to fight for you!
And now, let's give up the floor to the star reporter of the Crystal Daily!
So, honorary member! If you win the Holy Grail, what wish would you want granted?
rows.speaker: Reporter

rows.text: Why are you two even here?
Why are you both acting as reporters?
It's an "ace" up their sleeve, not "mace"!
You betcha.

I promised Pitch-Dark Hook the Great we'd record every thrilling moment of this trip to the Planet of Festivities for the folks back home. And here we are — stumbling upon you being interviewed for the Penaconian Holy Grail War—
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: I see. I was just wondering why someone else was taking my job, considering our channel secured exclusive rights to this interview and broadcast. Security, clear the area!
rows.speaker: Hostess

rows.text: We can talk this out... How about a collaboration!
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: Hey, hey, even the money-loving Alfalfa Family wouldn't charge such a cute kid a licensing fee, right?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Miss, consider it charity! Let this kid finish her "social studies project." I mean, what's the harm in that?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Assistant, get these two out of here!
rows.speaker: Hostess

rows.text: The assistants surged forward without warning, "escorting" the two foreign visitors far from the scene.
The Alfalfa Family proudly presents the First Penaconian Holy Grail War! We'll be following the Masters every step of the way, bringing you the freshest, most exclusive coverage.
rows.speaker: Hostess

rows.text: Before we continue our interview with the Nameless about the Penaconian Holy Grail War, let's cut to a quick commercial break—
rows.speaker: Hostess

rows.text: Ladies and gentlemen... I'm sure you've all heard the legend of the Holy Grail, haven't you?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Across the vast cosmos, such tales abound: seekers embarking on grueling journeys in pursuit of a miracle capable of turning their deepest desires into reality.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Yet, only a rare few ever have the privilege of witnessing its existence firsthand. Hohohoho! But today, I bring you all that very opportunity—
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: I have brought the omnipotent wish-granting chalice, the Holy Grail, to Penacony!
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Of course, the right to make a wish is a privilege beyond measure. And like most competitions in life, if you want to claim your reward, you'll have to fight for it!
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: The Holy Grail will summon Heroic Spirits — legendary figures from Penacony's rich history and bring them back to life. And you, daring Dreamchasers, will become Masters, commanding these Servants in battle until only one survivor remains!
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Worried it sounds a bit violent? Afraid it might turn into another Taikiyan Roboball competition with limbs flying and blood spattering everywhere?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Fear not! Mark my words: in the sweet dream of Penacony, there is no such thing as death! Any violence you witness is nothing more than harmless spectacle. The only thing real... is the prize of having your wish come true!
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: After all, this is the planet of chasing dreams. Here in Penacony, anyone with a dream in their heart has a chance to make it a reality.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Now, brought to you by the Alfalfa Family and proudly sponsored by SoulGlad™, the high-stakes battlefield where dreams are on the line—
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: The first-ever Penaconian Holy Grail War! Let the games begin!
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Don't get me wrong, Mr. Oti... I'm honored you picked me, but I'm just a nobody, a bottom-tier cog in the IPC. And if the rumors are true, you're not exactly a fan of the IPC. So why me?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: I sent invitations to Penacony's top shareholders and family heads, welcoming them to join this Holy Grail War. Some accepted. Others turned their noses up, dismissing my carefully orchestrated spectacle as just a marketing stunt.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Seems like living in luxury has dulled the ambitions of the so-called elite. But underdogs like you? You're a whole different story. Now, remind me again. What wish would you make to the Grail?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Me, Skott? I'm just a lowly grunt trying to climb to a {RUBY_B#Headquarters Officer}P45 corporate rank{RUBY_E#}!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Hohoho! What a delightfully mundane wish! You aren't even dreaming of rubbing shoulders with legends like "Diamond" or something...
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: But compared to lofty nonsense like world peace, your dream is refreshingly grounded.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: So, the Holy Grail... Can it really grant my wish?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Of course it can! Kid, the Command Spell branded onto your hand is proof of your qualification. You've also summoned a Servant and witnessed their power for yourself.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Well, we are in a dream world where ice cream talks, wine bottles sing, and instruments play themselves. A Grail that grants wishes and legendary figures resurrecting from history? Not so far-fetched here, I guess.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: But here's the bigger question: If the Grail is real, why are you sharing it? Why turn this into a... show? Let's face it. If I were in your shoes, I'd keep it to myself, make my wish quietly, and get filthy rich.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Hohohoho! A sharp question, Skott. Let me put it this way: Picture an old man who's survived ten Amber Eras, navigated countless conspiracies and power struggles, accumulated an endless fortune, and climbed to the absolute pinnacle of Penacony...
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Now, tell me. What's left for such a person to wish for?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Uh... more money and power? No one ever thinks they've got too much of either, right? I don't know. You tell me, Mr. Oti.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Hohohoho! You're already getting close, kid.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: But a single wish? That's far too small to satisfy me. I want to transform the Holy Grail War into an unprecedented form of entertainment in Penacony! Imagine meeting historical legends, summoning them as Servants to fight for you, and finally making your wildest dreams come true.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: This will be Penacony's next grand spectacle, standing alongside the Charmony Festival as a beacon for the universe's attention. Dreamers and wealth beyond measure will pour in, far more than ever before!
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: And for the first-ever Holy Grail War, what story could be more compelling than the wish of a nobody coming true? Understand now?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: I get it now. Don't worry, Mr. Oti. I won't let you down. As a lone wolf, I've learned how to survive, no matter how desperate things are.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: But I'm not gonna lie, Mr. Oti... Just now, during that broadcast, I saw someone. Someone who's dragged me down to rock bottom more times than I can count. Funny how fate works. {F#She's}{M#He's} here on this battlefield, too.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Emm... Let me guess. You mean that Nameless from the Astral Express? A real showboat and a tough competitor, I'd say.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Yeah, in terms of pure strength? The old me couldn't compete with that monster and {M#his}{F#her} crew. But the person I am today? I'm not the same man I was back then.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: As a Master, survival hinges on using your summoned Heroic Spirits, your Servants, wisely, and utilizing their Noble Phantasms. Isn't that correct, Mr. Reca?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: While the Holy Grail War is ongoing, please address me as Grady, {RUBY_B#Master}Producer{RUBY_E#}.
Actually, during this War, he should call you by the code name "Assassin."
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: You're right. In the current Penacony, the name Grady carries no weight. Best not to bring it up.
Hohohoho! You got a chance at a second life. It's best to let go of fragile pride, old friend.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Names tie you to your past. They also expose your weaknesses. A wise competitor hides their true self from the opposition.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Listen up: I had to offer him film credits and the chance to experience a Heroic Spirit's memories just to convince {RUBY_B#Mr. Reca}that director{RUBY_E#} to {RUBY_B#Spirit Origin Fusion}act as your vessel{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: You've always dreamed of creating a masterpiece that would shake the world and cement your name in history, haven't you? On that point, you and Mr. Reca share the same goal. Don't waste the opportunity I've created for you...
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Go record the stories of the participants in this Holy Grail War, and help this ambitious young man by your side fulfill his wish!
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Following my Master's command, my Noble Phantasm has already been trained on those you invited. I can show their movements to you both in real time.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Well done, Assassin. With an ability like this, we're sure to stay ahead of the competition!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: The participants who have accepted the invitation and plan to join the Holy Grail War are already under my Noble Phantasm's watch. So producer, which one do you want to check out first?
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Using memory bubbles as invitations... a very Penaconian thing to do.
rows.speaker: Jade

rows.text: But what's even more Penaconian is this "omnipotent wish-granting chalice." Listen to that. Doesn't it sound like a cheap business scam? Only someone from a backwater place like Jarilo-VI could be fooled by a trick like that.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: ...Old Oti's serving up the "nectar," but what kind of "poison" is mixed into the cup?
rows.speaker: Jade

rows.text: Madam Jade, don't tell me you're actually trying to figure out what kind of game this old man is playing?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Why not? Penacony's biggest tycoon throws away his usual image of polite deal-making to invite the Family heads and shareholders to participate in this dream contest, promising afterward to grant a wish that someone could never fulfill on their own... Isn't that fascinating?
rows.speaker: Jade

rows.text: Fascinating? People with real power wouldn't waste a second of their time on something like this. Who would lower themselves just to entertain him? And if this so-called Holy Grail turns out to be nothing but a marketing gimmick, things are gonna get really interesting.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Old Oti knows that better than anyone. So what kind of return is big enough for him to risk the Alfalfa Family's entire reputation?
rows.speaker: Jade

rows.text: So, you believe this "omnipotent wish-granting chalice" might actually be real.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Across the cosmos, ceremonies that tap into a Path's power to create "miracles" aren't uncommon. The Credit Contracts I make with people. Aren't they a form of wish fulfillment, too? And even more so... are the Cornerstones we received.
rows.speaker: Jade

rows.text: So, does that mean you're interested in accepting the invitation?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: I am interested in the Holy Grail War, but not in the Grail itself. What intrigues me are the people who'd join this War for a so-called "miracle."
rows.speaker: Jade

rows.text: Placing your hopes and dreams on some unknown Holy Grail... it's like dousing yourself in oil and diving straight through a ring of fire.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Doesn't look promising. But it'll be one hell of a show.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: And more than that, it's the perfect opportunity to watch and make connections. Only one lucky fool will walk away with the Grail. But the Bonajade Exchange. No, the IPC's Strategic Investment Department can grant everyone's wishes.
rows.speaker: Jade

rows.text: Our future strategy calls for more allies. Aventurine, you're going to accept the invitation and join the Holy Grail War, aren't you?
rows.speaker: Jade

rows.text: I knew it. Penacony and I just can't seem to stay apart. But I have to say, the way they {RUBY_B#Command Spell}mark{RUBY_E#} the participants... not exactly pleasant.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Speaking of allies, a {RUBY_B#Boothill}certain someone{RUBY_E#} has returned to Penacony. Obviously, we can't have any official dealings with him... but since you've exchanged intel before, there's a little trust between you two.
rows.speaker: Jade

rows.text: I want you to use this Holy Grail War as a chance to strengthen that trust.
rows.speaker: Jade

rows.text: As you wish.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: "Mr. Pom-Pom," it's been a while~
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Hah! Now that's forkin' hilarious. Girl, I know my identity's a little... touchy. But here in Dreamflux Reef, just call me by my name, alright?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: It sure has been a while since we last saw each other. Not since that monkey raised hell here. How'd your agent even let a big-time star like you put on a street performance like this?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: A true singer doesn't only perform for the ones who can afford front-row seats.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: But you, Mr. Boothill, your appearance here means something big's about to go down again in Dreamflux Reef, doesn't it?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Hey now, don't go makin' me sound like some kind of walking disaster siren! You've heard of the Holy Grail War, right? The ads are everywhere. Nobody in Penacony could've missed it.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Wait... are you telling me you're joining the Holy Grail War?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Huh? Why do you sound so shocked? Am I not supposed to?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: That's not what I meant... or maybe that is what I meant...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: As far as I know, only The Family heads, IPC execs, and the Astral Express crew received invitations to this Holy Grail War — basically, the "decision-makers" of Penacony.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: And ain't I, "Pom-Pom," a member of the Astral Express?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: That's not what I am saying!
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Hah, relax, I'm just messin' with you. For some reason, that old man went and sent an invitation to Dreamflux Reef too. Micah figured things might go down the same way they always do — the folks up top have their fun, and the people below take the hits.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: So he sent me the invite, said I might be interested.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: I see... So Mr. Micah's asking for your help, in his own way.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Makes sense. I mean, after all I'm a two-time hero of Penacony! Sunday, the monkeys...
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Ahh, dadgum, my stupid mouth. Why'd I bring that up? Sorry. Listen, I don't care about any muddle-fudgin' Holy Grail, but a Holy Grail War? Now that sounds dangerous.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Yeah... I get that feeling too.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Summoning dead guys from their graves to duke it out, winner takes all? That sounds like something those IPC shirtbags would come up with. No heckin' way I vibe with that kinda setup.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: But since I took Micah's request, I gotta see this through. Make sure things don't spiral out of control.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Alright, time to get prepped. Up next, per the invite's instructions... summoning a Heroic Spirit. See ya!
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Who the heck keeps tossing garbage around? The next passenger Pom-Pom catches littering is going to have to write down the train's sanitation rules, a hundred times!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Huh? The First Penaconian Holy Grail War? Inviting the Astral Express to join? Sounds like the kind of spectacle that might interest you, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Hmm... Seems like {F#s}he's not around. Maybe I should pass this to March and Dan Heng instead — wait, why is there graffiti on Pom-Pom's hand!?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Ugh... it won't come off!? Who's behind this prank?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: The stage is set, and the characters are all in position. But, Master, for you and me, this Holy Grail War comes with a few... complications.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Yeah, the competition this time is no joke.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: No, what I mean is... If you look at the backstories of the participants, they generally fall into three categories: {RUBY_B#Aventurine}those who are in direct competition with your department{RUBY_E#}, {RUBY_B#Boothill}those who have a personal grudge against your department{RUBY_E#}, and {RUBY_B#Nameless}those who see you as their sworn enemy{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: In other words, from a narrative standpoint, every single participant we've identified so far is likely to target you first.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: It's us. You call that a *IPC profanity* "complication"? Like I didn't already know everyone here has a bone to pick with me?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: A little personal wisdom: Not everyone is your enemy, kid. Learn to separate "conflict of interest" from "personal vendetta."
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: And the key difference? The first one can be negotiated. The second? Not so much. So if I were you...
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: You'd deal with the personal vendettas first. Heh, heh. Much appreciated, Mr. Oti. I'll keep that in mind.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: What a poetic twist... Old rivals now destined to settle the score on the Holy Grail War's stage.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Lucky for me, I drew the best possible card: Assassin! With your Noble Phantasm, we should have the upper hand...
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: That said, knowing your opponent's next move isn't enough. It's like having a script but never actually shooting the film. Let me remind you, Master. Your least-favorite Nameless is preparing the ritual to summon a Servant right now...
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Heh heh, [Trailblazer], I gotta take care of you first. Can't have any loose ends hanging around.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Wait... You're telling me the Strategic Investment Department is joining, too!?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: What's wrong, Mr. Skott? As a member of the Marketing Development Department, their reach shouldn't extend to you, right?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: That's right, Mr. Oti. Besides, with you backing me up, even Louis Fleming...
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Hohohoho... Let's just let Louis Fleming rest for now.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: That guy... That's the wanted criminal Boothill!?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Mr. Oti, sir, c—can't you revoke his qualification? Letting a criminal join the Holy Grail War is way too dangerous! What if he wishes for every single IPC employee to drop dead? That'd be the end of us!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Kid, you're basically admitting you think that cowboy's going to win the whole thing. Where's your confidence? You gotta keep your head in the game.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Once you accept the invitation and are branded with the Command Spells, your qualification as a Master can't be revoked.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Then we should send out the Bloodhounds and take that criminal down immediately!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Hohoho~ But Mr. Boothill wasn't wrong, was he? He's saved Penacony twice before. If we jump the gun and hunt him down now, that wouldn't be very... tactful.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: ...Why are you so scared of this guy, Skott?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Uh... let's just say there's some personal history. He's got a, uh... particularly brutal way of handling my department's people...
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Hohoho~ Then isn't this your perfect shot at vengeance? Win this war, and you can bring that cocky cowboy crashing down yourself.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Heh... Don't worry, Mr. Oti. Forget a small fry like Boothill. If the traps are set right and the schemes are airtight, even Louis Fleming wouldn't be able to escape!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Tsk, the world's turned upside down... Even the animals on the Astral Express can enter this tournament!?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Mr. Oti, should I take care of this first?
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: No need~ Letting a contestant like them compete just makes things even more interesting!
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Now that's more like it. Let's move out!
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Let's move out!
Give me a moment.
I'll protect everyone to the best of my ability. Please don't stray too far from me. But with the enemy in the shadows and us out in the open, even the greatest caution can't guarantee our safety.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: If this is a decoy, the real enemy's probably lurking nearby, waiting for us to take the bait. We should steer clear of this trap.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Skott? The IPC Specialist who does those bionic voice impressions?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Seriously? It's not the time for this!
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: A director of flops from centuries ago catching the eye of a big shot from the Strategic Investment Department? Thanks for the compliment, but that was a pretty bad lie from you.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Come to think of it, wasn't there someone else? Not far away, he is slowly slipping away with hushed steps.
I reserve judgment on your film taste.
No wonder you know his films so well.
Wait, weren't you the one who roasted him so hard before?
Tsk, aren't we supposed to meet up here? [Trailblazer]... where did they go?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: ...Something's off. Maybe someone got the jump on them and took {M#him}{F#her} and {M#his}{F#her} Servant out before we got here.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: With all due respect, if that hypothetical enemy could easily defeat your friend's Saber, then none of us here would be walking away alive.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Or maybe our old friend is concerned about {RUBY_B#my}an IPC employee{RUBY_E#} showing up, so they're lurking in the shadows to assess us?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Oh? Were you enemies once?
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Past enemies can still become present-day allies. Am I right, cowboy?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Even with the IPC, {F#s}he should at least trust me after we went through so much together. Hey, [Trailblazer]! Come on out! Let's chat about joining forces as a team! You ain't gonna get hurt!
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: They aren't coming. I went through a lot of possibilities in my head before we got here, but I never expected to face the most ridiculous of them all...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: ...A shirtbag pulled off a scam on a Galaxy Ranger.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Listen up, forkin' shirtbags! Ain't no matter who you are and what you wanna do, I've got you surrounded! Pop out now, or don't say I didn't warn ya when you stub your toe on the way to the underworld!
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Did you hear that? He's gonna kill us if we don't give ourselves up. Oh, he's every inch a serious criminal with a huge bounty on his head. I'm positively shaking in my boots with how he talks...
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Wait! Isn't that... Isn't that Mr. Aventurine of the Ten Stonehearts!? Why is a criminal wanted by the IPC walking around with an IPC executive?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Sir! If that blasted cowboy's got you kidnapped at gunpoint, just gimme a blink! Or... or maybe... you two are actually friends?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: "An IPC Executive Secretly in Cahoots With a Cosmic Fugitive" — Assassin, you've got to grab this awesome scene on film.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Your Servant is... Mr. Reca? No... Now that I'm looking at him, there's something off...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Hey. You know him? The guy in the IPC uniform next to Reca?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: There are more IPC employees who know my face than there are grains of sand in Sigonia's desert. You think I can remember them all?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Wretched brat! You think I'm scared of you just cos you're a Stoneheart? The Strategic Investment Department's reach may be long, but it will never reach my neck of the woods!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: After I win the Holy Grail, I will make everyone do as I say! I'll make you all kneel before me and beg for mercy, then have you bark like dogs, oink like pigs... no! Croak like frogs!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: What a waste. Using the Holy Grail to make people do animal noises.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: So Old Oti even sent invitations to your department? But I thought you folks barely stationed anyone at Penacony. Unless... unless your name is...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Huh!? H—Have you actually heard of me?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Hmm. Never mind. There's no way I'd ever remember the name of some nobody.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Ha! You high and mighty executives have never treated us basic workers as people! You would send me to a primitive post like the Xianzhou with one word, and switch me over to Penacony with the next! I thought Penacony might be a juicy gig...
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: ...But all I've done every day is talk business to a bunch of Pepeshi! It's making my neck crank even worse!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: But hey, all of that will soon be a thing of the past. Aventurine? Heh, I'll replace you and become the new Stoneheart of that name!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Assassin! Use your Noble Phantasm to bring me victory!!!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: It's unusually quiet. No sign of Mr. Boothill or the enemy who lured us here.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: In a wide-open area like this, if the enemy sends Archer to attack from range, we'll lose the initiative and be at a serious disadvantage.
rows.speaker: Saber
