rows.text: From what I know of Old Oti, he's the type to hire the lowest scum as his pawn, summoning the most wicked Servant to eliminate anything in his way.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Haven't you noticed? Since earlier, our voices vanish when we speak.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: *Clears throat*
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: That's true... Could it be the enemy's so-called Noble Phantasm?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: More importantly, everyone, I have a question. In this world's history, is it possible for a non-primate to become a Heroic Spirit? Say, a billboard? Or maybe a TV?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: If it were an Intellitron... that's at least plausible. But a billboard? A TV...?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Then what's that thing up ahead...?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: A TV, appearing out of nowhere, turns its polished rear to the crowd.
Creak, creak, creak.
rows.speaker: Mysterious TV

rows.text: It's obviously a trap...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: A frigid force drags you violently back to where you started. And then, a voice you know all too well murmurs by your ear.
You want to leave after entering Boss Skott's turf? In your dreams!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Unbelievable. Skott's really made a name for himself, even the acclaimed Robin knows who he is.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...Alright, I'm the one who told her. Can't a {M#guy}{F#gal} share a few wild travel stories with {M#his}{F#her} friends every now and then?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: The brief silence that lingers between you was enough to convey every ounce of fury and exasperation from this old acquaintance.
See? Always so hasty.
The battered TV wobbles, buzzing with static noise. But alas, this is a silent film. You can't hear a single crackle of the snowflakes.
Watch out for his Servant! That guy turned this whole place into—
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Supporting characters with no voice dubbing shouldn't waste the audience's time with your lines.
rows.speaker: Assassin

rows.text: Ready... ACTION!
rows.speaker: Assassin

rows.text: Why do actors in horror films never see where the monsters come from? Why do monsters keep popping into the frame as long as the film is rolling?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: It's because the true monster is born beyond the set. The director's lens... is the real cradle of terrors.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Your Presence Concealment skill is simply a manifestation of the theatrical rule that characters in the story cannot see the cinematographer filming behind the lens.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: But monsters are different. They are the soul of horror films, the focus of the lens. Their line of sight is always fixed on the camera's position. That's why only Skott, the man playing the monster... can see you.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: You win... I concede.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Having the devil lurking behind the lens and getting real monsters to step into the theater, that was my finest offline marketing campaign ever. Who'd have thought that someone could still see through my tricks hundreds of years in the future?
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: How did you do it, friend?
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Did I never mention it to you? I'm your fan, Mr. Grady.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Have more confidence in yourself, Mr. Grady. After I stumbled upon your first movie, curiosity led me to dig through the archives of Grady Films.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Now, you had each moviegoer sign a death and liability release waiver before entering the theater... And you released Memory Zone Memes into the theater at intermission... These interactive marketing tactics were way ahead of their time.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: You could smell out exact market demands and deliver maximum impact with minimal resources. Had we met back then, I would've made sure to secure a spot for you in the marketing department.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Heh. I'd rather not be recognized for THOSE achievements.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: You could've been rolling in riches, but you poured everything into filmmaking to create something you loved. You're a director worthy of respect for that alone.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: But what you've done is unforgivable.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: The Watchmaker said almost the same thing to me back then. But like I said, I concede. I have no talent and can't create true art.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: I've come to terms with that after dying.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Then, could you tell us Old Oti's plan?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: If he truly wanted to achieve his wish, he could've easily hired a few Masters to stage a variety show with a rigged outcome.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: But he deliberately gathered a group of uncontrollable individuals to participate in a Holy Grail War that might never even happen.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Mr. Oti gave me a backup plan before I came here. When I lose, I'm to humbly admit defeat and invite everyone to the Grand Theater.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Mr. Oti and the Holy Grail will be waiting for you there. You'll hear all the answers from him.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: And you, my fan... this little behind-the-scenes is just for you. I believe the reason Mr. Oti reached out to you all is simple — You'll bring in higher ratings for this show.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Ho? Do I finally get to see this shrimp's Servant in action? Archer, get ready for a fight.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: What's with the happy smile?
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: The filming has begun, actors. Take your positions!
rows.speaker: Assassin

rows.text: Let the camera roll, let the film spin, and let us return to "The Silent Horror Picture Show"!
rows.speaker: Assassin

rows.text: Ready... ACTION!
rows.speaker: Assassin

rows.text: Wait, this isn't spirit form. He just vanished, right before our eyes. This Servant's Presence Concealment is more disturbing than I imagined. Wait—
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Where's your voice?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Where's my voice? Forkin' hell, forkin' hell! Son of a fork!
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: It's no use. I've tried analyzing this Bounded Field. It doesn't just mute sound, something far more dangerous is closing in.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: If there's no sound, then how'd you know what I just said?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Look, there are subtitles here.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Hahahahaha! I've always wanted to see you people like this! A bunch of idiots subjected to my every whim!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: That's not fair! Why do you get to have a voice?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: And why have you been reduced to this, may you ask? Because now I am the protagonist! You extras will never be treated in the same way as me! I can't wait to hear what kind of petrified screams you'd be making in this horror show...
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Oh. Wait. Oops, I forgot. No one can hear their own screams in Assassin's Noble Phantasm.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: A moment later, the cowboy's friends arrived, equally clueless.
We've crossed swords a few times in past Holy Grail Wars. Our allegiances often clashed, but... he's not a bad person.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: While the energy sustaining me does not seem to originate from you... there is, without a doubt, a connection between us.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: I've noticed that as well.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: No, I am no Heroic Spirit of this land. I've never even heard of a nation called Penacony in my world.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: The Holy Grail granted me the knowledge I need to participate in this war, but much of it makes no sense. This world... is completely foreign to me.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: It seems that, from the very foundation of our existence, we hail from two entirely different worlds.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Oh? Seems like different worlds have their share of strange parallels. Tell me, does your Camelot still stand?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: To help this Servant understand this dream world bathing in memoria, you go on a lecture about interstellar travel and cosmic geography.
Forgive me. I must seem rather undignified.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: My apologies. To think the first request I make of my new Master is to... devour a feast. Hardly befitting of a king's dignity.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Not at all. I've never been particular about taste. Besides, hunger is the best seasoning.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Come on! I'll take you to try the local specialty, Halovian Winged Burgers! No way your world has that!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Skott!? You again? Why is it always you?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Tell me, are you my Servant?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You think you can take a cheap shot and beat me just because my summoning failed?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Let's not waste time. Your summoning ritual just flopped. This is the perfect moment to serve you every ounce of humiliation you once dealt me, with interest.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Do I look like it?
Oh, don't thank me just yet. My plan was to take you out next.
Not a bad idea. But you see, I just hooked a big one.
You can call me Lancer.
Next up is the moment we've all been waiting for! [Trailblazer] will step in the summoning circle, chant the spell, and summon one of the greatest souls in Penaconian history!
rows.speaker: Hostess

rows.text: Who will it be? The legendary dreamweaver Glaux? Or perhaps the first Bloodhound? Let's find out!
rows.speaker: Hostess

rows.text: The stage is set. Now, step into the summoning circle and begin the ritual.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: These useless mooks are even worse than I thought. Anyways, just fall back for now.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Skott, that's all you've got?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You really had the guts to chase me down, huh, [Trailblazer]?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: What a shame. Your Holy Grail War ends right here.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Target is in position! Ready, Assassin?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Ready to roll, producer!
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: A blood-splattered, interstellar slasher comedy. Action!
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: You? Tch... What a terrible reunion.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: That's what I was thinking too, Lancer. But as long as I stand here, I won't let you lay a hand on my Master.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Well, kid... you just hit the jackpot.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: It's safe now, Master. Are you hurt?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Wait, you two know each other?
Are you my Servant?
Yes, you are my Master. And I am your Servant.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: You don't... seem to be from this world.
Are you from Penacony?

Ah, I forgot to introduce myself. You may call me by my Servant class, Saber, or by my True Name, Altria Pendragon. I was once the King of Knights in Camelot. I assume you know nothing about this place either?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Not a thing.
We do have a Camelot here, actually.

Unfortunately... no. It was completely destroyed. But there are still survivors. I have a friend from there, {RUBY_B#Guinaifen}Guinevere{RUBY_E#}. She's got an older brother named {RUBY_B#Langshile}Lancelot{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Wait, what???
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Guinevere's... brother... Lancelot? You mean like, biologically related?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: You know what? Let's just put a pin in that for now. Clearly, our worlds have some serious differences.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Only to suddenly hear a thunderous rumble... It seems the lady knight before you is starving.
Was that thunder?
You may not realize it, but this world has almost no magical energy.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: And as a Heroic Spirit from a completely unknown realm, I can't draw power from "fame" or Mystics. So, to maintain my combat strength... I need a lot of energy intake.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Master. Do you know anywhere around here that serves large portions?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: You really don't have to explain all that...
Well, if you're not picky about the food...
At the same time, in the Golden Hour.
Come forth from the circle of binding, Guardian of the Scales!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You waited for a while, but nothing happened.
So... Where's the Servant?
rows.speaker: Hostess

rows.text: There was no light pollution, no exciting music, and no soul that came down from the sky. There was only an awkward silence.
Where's my Servant???
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Oh, I wish I could capture this pathetic little moment of yours and pass it down as a family heirloom for generations.
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: I was actually worried you'd luck out and summon some terrifying Servant... but turns out, you're just plain cursed!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Compared to you, even I seem less of a "lone wolf" now that I have a Servant. Maybe I should let you borrow the title for a couple of days. Bwahaha!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: What, you think I came all this way just to get payback? Oh, don't flatter yourself!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: I'm here to chase my dream! I don't care about you! At all! Seriously, your existence has zero impact on my mental state! None! Nada! Not at all! I'm completely unbothered! Totally!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: What!? Obviously not! I'm your opponent, fool! Do you seriously not recognize me!?
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Listen up, {M#lad}{F#girlie}, let me teach you why rules matter. This is the Holy Grail War! Having a Servant versus fighting alone? That's the difference between wearing power armor and charging in shirtless!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: But hey, I'm a fair guy. Since you failed to summon a Servant... I won't use mine to beat you either. Boys, go get 'em!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: That spear... What just happened? It wiped the field!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Don't tell me this guy's your Servant! Assassin, do something!
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Someone's crashed the set. Producer, I'm not built for front-line combat. And that guy is bad news. So, how about we take the smart approach and run?
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Hmph. So he put his Master into spirit form too. Assassin-class... always such a pain in the neck.
That's not my True Name, of course, but since you'll be out of the game soon... well, does it even matter?
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Farewell, Master-with-no-Servant.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: The Silent Stage: Act I
Midnight Chainsaw Rhapsody
Lead Actors
The Silent Stage: Act II
A Haunting of Clocks
Lead Actors
Hmph... An endless corridor. A layout completely different from before. What an annoying Bounded Field.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: If we can't bring this space to calm, we might never find a way out.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Producer! You useless piece of junk! I sent you to ambush two mere low-threat characters, how did you still mess that up?
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: And this music... Why can't my Noble Phantasm suppress it?
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Looks like you've been dead for too long. Forgot your own trade, huh? Even in the silent film era, movies had soundtracks.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: A forgotten piece of history... is no help to us now.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Forget that third-rate nobody, what I really want to know is: Where did he send our Servants? Splitting up in a horror movie? That's a death flag. Let's figure out what we're dealing with here.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Master? I saw your subtitles! I'll find a way to get you out!
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: By Xipe! I did not expect someone your age to know that much about Penacony's early dream bubble cinema. You have a bright future ahead.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: As expected. Soon, you'll see who Penacony's greatest director is. For now, I'll slip behind the scenes.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Let's vote. I vote for my flamboyant Master.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: As the star of this film, I'll be the one to personally tear you all apart, limb by limb!
rows.speaker: Chainsaw Skott

rows.text: Right. He was a film director in life. That means he's not gonna suddenly become a powerhouse after turning into a Heroic Spirit.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: You see that, Master? Looks like Miss Robin's alliance is starting to come together. This army has a goal, and now it's time to move.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Whatever you have in mind, it's already too late.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: We meet again. As a Caster, your combat style... was quite a surprise.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Let's just say... it was unpleasant.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Private disagreements? You ruined my life! You made me bark and oink and face a demotion, moving from one puny post to another in the cosmos in despair and misery... And this is what you call it? "Private disagreements"!?
rows.speaker: Thousand-Faced Skott

rows.text: Young and didn't know what you were doing? You ruined my life! You made me bark and oink and face a demotion, moving from one puny post to another in the cosmos in despair and misery... And this is what you call it? "Young and didn't know what you were doing"!?
rows.speaker: Thousand-Faced Skott

rows.text: Make it up to me? You ruined my life! You made me bark and oink and face a demotion, moving from one puny post to another in the cosmos in despair and misery... And this is all you have to say? "Make it up to me"!?
rows.speaker: Thousand-Faced Skott

rows.text: [Trailblazer]... and your little entourage of extras... you won't get to be cocky for much longer...
rows.speaker: Thousand-Faced Skott

rows.text: Grady! Are you trying to betray me? Don't forget, I am your Master. With my Command Spell, you'll have to — ribbit? Ribbit, ribbit? Ribbit? Ribbit!
rows.speaker: Multiple Skott

rows.text: You all wake in a sealed chamber, the TV's static crackle singing death's lullaby.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Separated from your Servants, you run into another pair of familiar enemies. As for your cowboy and songstress companions? Vanished without a trace.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Why are you here?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Skott sent a scam text to Mr. Boothill in your name, and you know how that goes.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: That monster in the room sure is an eyesore.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: I can't believe that even you fell for it, Archer.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Just so we're clear, I was against this from the start. But those two blockheads insisted on investigating.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Now it's three blockheads. Masters of an otherworldly Holy Grail War, and not a hint of caution among them... That's how I end up with frown lines.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Isn't it a little late to say all that? Listen carefully, "This place—"
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: This Holy Grail War is strange indeed. It's my fault, I have failed as a Servant. I should've kept my Master away from this trap.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Hold on. If I were the enemy, I'd disguise myself as a Master and wait just behind that door for the perfect ambush.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Archer, listen to my voice! It's obviously me, right?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Sorry, this is a silent film. All I see is a line of subtitles under the door, with the name "Aventurine" slapped on it. If you want to prove you're really my Master, you'll have to spill ten humiliating secrets that only my real Master would know.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: You really don't know who I am?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Will this ever end!? This is a horror film, people! Background characters, start acting scared!
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: "This place was once an IPC prison, where criminals were banished. Its deadly traps ensured none escaped. Now, the inmates have passed, leaving only bloodthirsty, vengeful spirits."
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: I've wanted to ask this since your first line. Why target the IPC Workers?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Back when this was still a prison, the IPC scoundrels turned it into a living hell. What do audiences love most? Watching those criminals suffer.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Saw off someone's leg, and the door unlocks automatically. But, if nothing happens after a system hour—
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: BOOM! The room explodes. You, the guests, will also go up in flames.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: I know this one! "The room you can't leave unless you do a particular thing!" It's one of the classic tropes from Penacony's vintage horror flicks!
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: That's right! I was the one who gave the world my genius vision with my first film in Penacony's early days!
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: So this "Noble Phantasm" is based on that? This guy's really getting carried away and started babbling... Nice work, Master.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: No wonder the scene feels so awkwardly shoved in. Now it all makes sense. Randomly cobbling together old-school horror tropes? Yeah, not exactly groundbreaking.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Take that "sawing off someone's leg" bit. Originally, the protagonist was restrained by ferrofluid shackles, and had no choice but to cut their own leg off. But here? It's just a lazy copy-paste.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Kid, I take back every compliment I said about you. Your screams will be played on loop in the most conspicuous spot at Grady Films.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Revealing your True Name on purpose. Let me guess, just part of your dramatic flair, huh?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Y—You fool! How did you let your True Name slip like that? Isn't that supposed to be a Heroic Spirit's greatest weakness? Assassin!?
rows.speaker: Skott's Voice

rows.text: Uh... don't panic, Producer. I'm not some legendary hero or anything like that. Just ask them. What does "Grady" even mean in Penacony?
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: So, what will it be? Self-sacrifice? Or will you turn your blades at each other right before my eyes? Take what little time you have left and talk it over. But keep stalling, and well — tick, tock... BOOM.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Master, stay close to me. I don't know what that Assassin plans to do next... But it's still dangerous here.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Using brute force in a horror film? Heroic Spirits from another world clearly have no sense of art!
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: A blonde beauty like you. Shouldn't you be screaming for help and waiting for the hero to save the day?
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Skulking Assassin, once I reach you, scream all you want, call for anyone to save you.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Then you'd better reach me first! Thanks to your recklessness, "the hotel's chainsaw spirit has been awakened by the noise." Protagonist, take the stage!
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Kekekeke... Trying to run? Did I, the protagonist, ever gave you permission to run!?
rows.speaker: Chainsaw Skott

rows.text: This... What kind of evil spirit gets beaten to a pulp by its victims? ...Ugh, forget it. Producer, take five. We'll be needing you again later.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Wait—!
rows.speaker: Chainsaw Skott

rows.text: So this is the power of Heroic Spirits from another world? ...Hmph. Figures. Penacony's just a backwater speck with ten Amber Eras. With no real legend or history, of course we pale in comparison to true heroes.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: But that's also why you're going to lose. I'll take each of you runaways, one by one, and turn you into obedient extras for my film.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Pray tell, does anyone look like they're running from you?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Don't get ahead of yourselves. Act Two is about to begin.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: After a brief pause, you exchange the information you've gathered with one another.
Boothill, Robin, and Miss Note are all still missing. Skott and his Servant could strike again at any time.
So they're giving us time to breathe, huh? Guess they're pretty confident about their trump card.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Archer's Master, you seem very familiar with films. What do you know about this Grady?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: I've only heard the name before. The guy was some terrible director back in Penacony's early days. He cranked out a ton of cheap horror silent films and was a master of interesting commercial gimmicks.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: But people in Penacony forgot about his name ages ago. I only found the film he used to trap us through sheer luck — picked it up at an interstellar junk market.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: So... we're dealing with a total nobody? That's not good.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: What makes you say that?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: As Heroic Spirits who left a mark in history, our legends usually hint at our greatest weaknesses — like that one warrior who bathed in the river of the underworld and became invincible except for his heel.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: I was hoping you'd know something about that person's past. But turns out he's just some washed-up no-name that even you folks have not heard about.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Fits right in with Mr. Skott, doesn't it? A pair of nobodies with shady tricks up their sleeves.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Still, I've got this feeling... even if they've got the upper hand now, they've got no real way to finish us.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: His Noble Phantasm proves it. He built it off one of his old horror flicks — basically a Reality Marble. Though it's a rare ability, it feels more like a trap, one that only ensnares its victims.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: ...But if the trap can't hurt the prey, then it's the hunter who'll be in trouble.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Now he's got three Servants in his stomach, while the strongest fortresses always fall from the inside.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: ...You really do have the mind of a leader, always so sharp on reading the situation.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: I'd better pull my weight too. He might not have an obvious weak spot, but if we can find Assassin's true body and let my arrows give him a proper haircut, that Reality Marble of his would no longer exist.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: *clap hands* Sounds like everyone's got their sights set.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: [Trailblazer], I know I've butted heads with the Express Crew before, but that was just a difference in perspective. As for this time, I've got no interest in the Holy Grail. My boss is more concerned about what Old Oti has up his sleeve.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: If you're willing... maybe we can actually work together this time?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: We saw the exit on the way in. Let's head that way while we still can.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Feels like we've just looped back to where we started...
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: If we don't find some kind of countermeasure, we could be stuck running in circles forever. Master, why not leave some of your chips and dice behind as markers?
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: You don't need to remind me of that. I've already tried it... But didn't expect Grady to be such a greedy money-grubber.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Hey, hey! Don't go throwing shade, extra boy! I was just cleaning up the set as usual. Gotta make sure random props don't ruin the scene.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: The next scene is all about IPC employees trapped in a haunted hallway and cursed to suffer forever.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Nowhere to escape, and no one will ever come to help. In here, any struggle is just wasted effort.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Is that... Miss Robin's singing?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Grady, looks like you forgot that you didn't only trap US in your Noble Phantasm.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: That's what you get for cutting the budget, Grady. While you're busy writing, directing, and starring as yourself, Miss Robin already found the way out on the other side of the set.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Everyone, follow the music!
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: A gentle force of Harmony floats through the tight space. At its heart, two singers light the way for the lost.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: But at the same time, evil spirits approach them, determined to shred and consume these visitors from beyond the sky!
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: In a blur too fast to track, Miss Note grabs the attacking monsters and viciously smashes their head into the floor.
"Oh no! My cathode ray tubes! Ahh! Don't hit my screen with your microphone! Ow!" Clunk clunk clunk, bang bang bang.
Honestly, that might be the first R-rated scene in this whole movie. You start to wonder if Robin actually summoned a Berserker.
That's it? The guards back in Asdana Prison were tougher than these things.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Bravo! Truly Penacony's brightest bloom — brilliant in both drama and action.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: This terrible wardrobe, the nonsense plot... No one else could've cooked this up but you, Grady.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: I spent so much effort clawing my way out of the grave, so quit burning my eyes with your bargain-bin flicks!
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Of course... real directors know when to leave the stage to the actors.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Can't say that counted as a fight between mages... Guess people in Penacony really have a broad definition of Caster.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Really? I thought it was pretty normal.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: An Archer dual-wielding swords isn't qualified to talk about this.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: I managed to feel out the right path using the power of Harmony, all thanks to Miss Note's protection.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: ██████, I saw you covering me in that fight. Even if you can't say your name... I know you must be someone great. I believe in that wholeheartedly.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Master, this cannot change the present situation. Without a True Name, I'm just a weak Iris Family artist.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: No. The way you shielded your Master just now proves you're an exceptional Servant.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: You'll never understand the despair when even your name is taken away, and you've been wrung dry of all worth.

rows.text: Exactly. Powerless. Barely able to protect her Master, let alone win this Holy Grail War.

rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.speaker: Grady

rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Honestly, the way this guy keeps coming for you? Even the wildest British hounds would call it obsessive. Master, what did you do to him?

rows.speaker: Thousand-Faced Skott

rows.text: Master, your line! Say your entrance line!
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.speaker: Stubborn Skott

rows.speaker: Saber

rows.speaker: Grady

rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Did we just... leave his Reality Marble?

rows.text: I might give it a thought.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Too bad. I thought you were smarter than this. Guess you'll have to suffer for it.

rows.text: "The wicked Watchmaker brought from hell evil spirits that wield different curses, disguised as harmless amusement park mascots. They drag victims into sleep and torture their souls for eternity."

rows.text: Don't worry. Mr. Oti's PR team will handle it. I used to dream of turning Clock Studios Theme Park into my own nightmare park. Who knew I'd get my wish this way?

rows.text: I'm honestly as shocked as you are. Who'd have thought there's "justice" in that man called Skott? And yet, my chest burns with righteous fire.
rows.speaker: Skott of Justice

rows.text: Skott of Justice's not like those evil ones. He threw himself in to protect me, tweet!
rows.speaker: Origami Robin

rows.text: You trust this son of a nosewalker? Might as well believe I'm a general of the Xianzhou. No offense, but making someone like him turn over a new leaf is like asking the Antimatter Legion to plant trees in the Kingdom of Banditry.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: I completely agree. We can't afford the risk. If the enemy cursed him or turned him into some kind of special familiar, then...
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Then I thought... what if this is all part of Skott's plan? What if the evil side of him is lying in wait within me, ready to spring to action at any moment...
rows.speaker: Skott of Justice

rows.text: I want to go with you to save the other Miss Robins, and I also need someone to kill me if Skott ever takes over my body.
rows.speaker: Skott of Justice

rows.text: How about we take him in for now? If he turns good, great. If not, we can always chuck him at his Servant as a projectile.
rows.speaker: Ranger Robin

rows.text: Well, since the victim herself said so...
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: To honor the trust placed in me, I will never bend to evil. *ribbit*
rows.speaker: Skott of Justice

rows.text: Miss Ranger, we'll count on you to escort this... little bird back to Saber and the others. We'll wrap this up fast, find the rest of Miss Robin, and track down my unreliable Master.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: *ribbit* I'll prove my justice with my actions. *ribbit*
rows.speaker: Skott of Justice

rows.text: Before I judge you all, I must first deal with a disobedient pawn — Skott, how utterly despicable that you'd side with them.
rows.speaker: Old Clockie

rows.text: So desperate to play the hero, aren't you?
rows.speaker: Old Clockie

rows.text: Tch, just felt an ominous chill run down my spine.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Why waste your breath on it? One bullet to fudge them up, and we're done here!
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Tick-tock, thought I'd just play along in your little hero fantasy? Mr. Grady gave me a special bullet that never misses. One pull of this trigger, and the Master with the most dialogue will drop dead on the spot.
rows.speaker: Old Clockie

rows.text: DIE, [Trailblazer]!
rows.speaker: Old Clockie

rows.text: Skott took the fatal hit meant for you.
I... can't keep going with all of you... But I'll die happy... knowing that I gave my life for justice... to keep others safe...
rows.speaker: Skott of Justice

rows.text: There's...
rows.speaker: Skott of Justice

rows.text: There's no such thing as a Skott of Justice!
rows.speaker: Skott of Justice

rows.text: That "justice" is a part of the name. It doesn't mean anything! What do you think? How would you rate this shocking reveal. *ribbit*
rows.speaker: Skott of Justice

rows.text: Director! Heal me up! I worked so hard to lead them into the trap, and now you're shooting me in the butt!?
rows.speaker: Skott of Justice

rows.text: *Penacony profanity*, if your worthless scene-stealing self hadn't blocked that bullet, Old Clockie would've eliminated [Trailblazer] already. Who are you to have the audacity to act proud?
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: I sent you undercover to deliver a crushing blow at the story's climax. Instead? You couldn't even manage basic narrative structure. Even a child could tell you were putting on an act!
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Since you're so desperate for attention, congratulations, Mr. Skott — you're hereby demoted from actor to stage decoration!
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Hey, what about my butt!?
rows.speaker: Skott of Justice

rows.text: Tick-tock, what gave you the impression I was faking? My Clockwork has been ticking away this whole time.
rows.speaker: Old Clockie

rows.text: Well, who do we have here? A poor little thing. Trying to save your friend from a curse when you can't even protect yourself.
rows.speaker: Old Clockie

rows.text: Surprised your Clockwork is useless? Shocked? Confused? Well, of course you are.
rows.speaker: Old Clockie

rows.text: The power of your Clockwork comes from Clockie, but I am Old Clockie. When the junior meets the senior, it's only natural for you to fail.
rows.speaker: Old Clockie

rows.text: Now, it's time for the old man to teach the kid a lesson.
rows.speaker: Old Clockie

rows.text: A feeling beyond words clutches at your mind — not one of Clockwork's four different emotions. This is darker, heavier, like a silent quagmire.

Departed loved ones, betrayal by those you trusted most, the shadow of approaching death... These manufactured emotions burst in your heart, leaving just a black void that watches you with the empty eyes of a corpse—
You finished with your little show yet? I don't have time to play pretend with you.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Impossible! I used Clockwork to turn everyone's emotions to pure despair!
rows.speaker: Old Clockie

rows.text: Ugh, how trite. Your dialogue is straight from Villains 101. These pathetic attempts at manipulation are less effective than vultures squawking over a corpse.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: What took you so long? Was that whole silent-badass act really necessary?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Despair? Please. I've witnessed enough scenes of despair to submerge this entire playground of nightmare.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: I've seen corpses hanging from gallows that stretch like endless forests. I've witnessed the charred remains after doomsday battles where people became nothing more than ravenous beasts devouring each other...
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Just who... who in the world ARE you!?
rows.speaker: Old Clockie

rows.text: A hardworking guardian, though admittedly somewhat of a workaholic. I've seen far too many forms of despair... but to break me? Your fake illusions don't even come close!
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Tick-tock, cranking power to maximum! I refuse to accept that anyone could resist my Clockwork now!
rows.speaker: Old Clockie

rows.text: Ever seen bodies mangled under war chariots? Trace on!
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Don't get smug, the director will avenge me. I, I—
rows.speaker: Old Clockie

rows.text: Extra lines won't earn you extra pay.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: O, in that case, I'm dead.
rows.speaker: Old Clockie

rows.text: Good, now let's regroup with the others.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Oh, looks like you just crawled out of a tough fight.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Forkin' void song whale, now you decide to appear after we did all the work?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Well, I did do something, alright? Some evil spirit called the Revolver Governor got all clingy with me, insisted we play a game — and ended up losing ten years' worth of savings to me. Look, I even brought an old friend back with me.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Zzz... Zzz...
rows.speaker: Sleepy Robin

rows.text: After a short break, the scattered allies finally reconvened from across the set.
I had no idea so much was happening... Thank you for keeping my Master safe.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Hmph, I just didn't want to give Grady the satisfaction.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Let's save the thanks for later. Didn't that girl say if we brought all her split selves together, she could return to normal?
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: I proposed this theory assuming none of the Robins would be in a defect status.
rows.speaker: Scholar Robin

rows.text: There's a dissonance in the melody — Despair. You Old Clockie — dang it, Grady, what foul language are you having me use!?
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Anyway, the emotion affecting the last Master hasn't disappeared despite the enemy's demise.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Ignore whatever you see — these are just my internal doubts and won't hurt anyone else.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Now, rebuild a melody that's truly your own.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Thank you everyone for your help. Without you, I would definitely have been fudgin'— sorry, seems the consciousness-splitting effects haven't completely worn off.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Everyone, please come closer. I've decoded this film's melody. With a few adjustments, we should break free from Grady's Noble Phantasm.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Master, you gave me the chance to join the Holy Grail War, and I saved you once in return. We're now square.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: What a pleasant surprise — old friend, have you finally understood that who it is that can truly grant your wish?
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: The evil spirit must still be affecting you. Let me tune you properly—
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Master, you're far too kind-hearted, with no interest in the Holy Grail. That's why I must pursue this path myself.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Mr. Oti is a businessman through and through. His price will be astronomically high.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: And? Would you really betray your friends just to let me win the Holy Grail War?
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Here's some advice: While I'm still here, use a Command Spell to kill me — just like all those others who toyed with my fate.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: If this is beyond you, Miss Robin, then we must part ways here.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Is this a declaration of war? Since you're no longer Miss Robin's Servant, I have no reason to let a potential enemy walk away.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: I can tell you're still hesitating. Before I draw my blade, there's still time to change your mind.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Everyone, aren't you forgetting something? I'm still here!
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: My old friend has finally found her path to fulfilling her wish, and I won't let anyone block her way. You wanna escape my Noble Phantasm? Then I'll just have to add some more excitement!
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: The second screening has ended. See you in the final nightmare!
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Goodbye, Master. May your kindness never meet betrayal.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Director! What about my butt? My butt! My—!
rows.speaker: Skott of Justice

rows.text: I failed, just like how I failed in life. This is... a fitting end for a traitor.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: The performing arts had given you so much pain, Miss Note... Why did you choose to remain on Penacony's stage after leaving your prison?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Because... I still remember how the rough prisoners fell silent, and the crying children smiled whenever I started to sing. Those small moments made me feel free even in that iron cage.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: But Penacony has changed. After so many Amber Eras, it's become almost unrecognizable. And now, I am locked in this newly-forged prison.
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Anyway, it's time to end this. A Servant who betrayed their Master has no right to exist!
rows.speaker: Miss Note

rows.text: Then, as you wish...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Mother of Iris, you will no longer be controlled by anyone from this moment on. You will now only dance for yourself.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: This farce is nearing its end, but I hope you can step out of the Grand Theater before you disappear, and meet Penacony's artists. You are still a "hero" to them — No matter the slanders your name bears.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I sense a powerful force similar to magical energy... It seems the Holy Grail's holder is about to complete the ritual.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: The last two Servants left are Rider and Berserker. Which one will face us? Or will it be both? With the enemy already in possession of the Holy Grail, it looks like we're in for a brutal fight.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Master, I swear on this sword that I will protect you, no matter the cost.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Ohohoho! Looks like Lady Asna has failed. What a shame. She was just one step away from tearing the flame of dreams off the Servants, and tossing them into the Holy Grail as fuel.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: But that's the business world for you. No matter how capable your collaborator is, you've gotta handle the most critical parts yourself.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Old fudgehead. It's time to tell us what kind of stinkin' pie you're cooking up with this "Holy Grail War."
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Meanwhile, the Master and their Servants, freed from the dreamscape, stepped into the heart of the Grand Theater...
You practically have one foot in the grave... Don't tell me you're going to wish for immortality.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Oh, I've lived for ten Amber Eras already. As long as I give the word, my medical team can squeeze a few more years out of these old bones.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Three against two. The advantage is mine.
Then are you trying to crush your business rivals? I heard there's some bad blood between you and my Master.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Ohohoho! What a great misunderstanding! There are no enemies that can't be made into friends in the world of business!
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Good point, but I'm still very curious about your little scheme.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Mr. Oti, surely you wouldn't be like the mages I know, willing to forsake both life and humanity just to reach the root of all things?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: ...Miss, what you're talking about is something only the Genius Society would obsessively chase after.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: What's your real reason, then?
It couldn't possibly be for money, could it?
Hahaha... why not?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: I've been very clear about this from the start. The Charmony Festival met a hasty wrap, and Penacony needs a fresh economic boost. We need to create a business venture that will grab everyone's attention!
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: A Holy Grail that grants wishes is just the golden goose we need! If this ritual works, then Penacony will own a glorious show to keep the money rolling in for ten more Amber Eras, a carnival that even the Charmony Festival can't compete with!
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Even if I do have some personal objectives in this first-ever Penacony Holy Grail War... that's none of your concern.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Wealth that pops out of thin air will only lead to inflation! Financial growth can't be achieved by miracles. It requires precise balance and expert handling. I like money, but I don't like to play a numbers game.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: What I like is watching people swarm into Penacony, spending their entire fortunes just to buy a chance to enter the Holy Grail War! I like having Alfalfa credits pour out of the Gilded Hour, entering the Cosmic Exchange!
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: I like seeing my business rivals being crushed and manipulated, and then lose everything in the end! I like to acquire companies that I've never heard of, fusing them into my empire with a mere wave of my pen!
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Why don't you just ask the Holy Grail for cash?
The Golden Hour will set the prices for goods based on my desires, and the Blue Hour will craft Penaconian fashion based on my whims.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Do you honestly believe Penacony was built on empty ideas like "dreams" and "wishes"? No! What truly underpins and supports this city is what you deem "crude." It's the unending flow of money! On this rock called money, we have built the Planet of Festivities!
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: No matter what your plans may be, there can only be one victor in the Holy Grail War. Your actions in this farce have already placed every Servant squarely against you.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Now, we stand together before you, shrewd merchant.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: I just wanna finish what I didn't get to do a few hours ago. I'm sick and tired of fish heads — The head of this old desperate fogey with broken dreams is what I'd call a real trophy!
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: You see this evil man's old head as a trophy? I thought you had better taste than that, Lancer.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Ohohoho! It seems you're all eager to prepare for my demise. But since there can only be one winner in this game, how do you plan to decide the victor after I bow out?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Why don't we discuss... a collaboration instead? Whoever can eliminate the others shall have the chance to make their wish to the Holy Grail. I will give you that right.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: We can even formalize it with a contract — using precise, logical language to word our wishes, ensuring the Holy Grail fulfills everyone's desires... After all, isn't this the very moment you've all been fighting for, Masters and Servants?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: A Holy Grail that sullies everyone's wishes is just a counterfeit for us to smash to pieces. Isn't that right, Master?
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Shh. No peaceful resolutions, please.
Nah. We need to whip this fella's hind-end, THEN smash it to pieces.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Our opinions rarely align, but I'm fond of this idea. What do you think, Mr. Aventurine? It's nice to play as the hero of justice now and then, isn't it?
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: I've already been the scapegoat once today... So I'll pass this opportunity to Mr. Oti.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: My Master, it seems I won't be able to claim the Holy Grail for you.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: I trust your choice.
I must thank Miss Note's dream for showing me the truth... What truly matters is not the ending, but the journey we've taken to chase something and to deliver it from destruction.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: I don't need the Holy Grail. The wishes I did not fulfill will end here.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Ohohoho... If you are all so keen to make me your enemy, I suppose I'll have to become the final challenge on this variety show.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: The rules said a Master is supposed to summon a historical figure as their Servant to enter the Holy Grail War, but... who should I summon? This question has haunted me for quite some time...
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Should I get the washed-up director I sponsored? Or the legendary star whose name I purchased? No. No. No. They are not worthy of being my Servant...
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: That's when a thought crossed my mind... Why not summon myself? A person who's still standing strong after ten Amber Eras of business intrigue... Isn't this living legend staring back at me in the mirror?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: I used myself as the catalyst... I wanted to see how the business magnate Oti, reflected in the history of Penacony, would respond to my call as a Servant. I wanted to see how people truly view me in history.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: And have you got your answer?
A bug madly devouring wealth.
rows.speaker: "Old Oti"

rows.text: Pfft... Hehehe, hahahahahaha—
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: The answer really hurts. To them, I'm nothing but a parasite, sucking out the sap of Penacony's oak from the top —
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: That gentle force... it stopped every single monster...
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: That's why it's Epsilon's superstar!
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: The Silent Stage: Special Feature
The Golden Gatekeeper
Lead Actors
Were the critics right all along? Am I really a third-rate director who can only take flops? No! It cannot be!
rows.speaker: Self-deceiving Heart

rows.text: This was just a mistake. An accident! I know how to improve now. I... I'll prove myself with my next film!
rows.speaker: Self-deceiving Heart

rows.text: Face it. You'll never be able to make a film like that.
rows.speaker: Honest Heart

rows.text: Mr. Grady, how do you respond to certain media calling Outer Space 6 the number one worst film in the galaxy?
rows.speaker: Echoes of the Interview

rows.text: Over-the-top effects. A storyline in complete shambles. Costumes and props that should've been handled with care rushed and half-baked.
rows.speaker: Echoes of Movie Reviews

rows.text: The "Father of Penaconian Cinema"? More like a washed-up antique, a flop king who only knows to leech off trends.
rows.speaker: Echoes of the Audience

rows.text: Artistic ambition without the necessary skills to back it up... A common sight in the film industry.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: That robot up ahead, could it be the "strongest Servant" Grady was talking about? Better keep our guard up and approach carefully.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Film theory, cinematography... I've learned them all! Why can I still not make a film like that!?
rows.speaker: The Tell-Tale Heart

rows.text: The Watchmaker and Maeven... What did they do to deserve more fame than me, the pioneer of the entire industry!?
rows.speaker: The Tell-Tale Heart

rows.text: If only they never made those films... If only those films were... mine.
rows.speaker: The Tell-Tale Heart

rows.text: If only... I never gave up my copyright...
rows.speaker: The Tell-Tale Heart

rows.text: Apologies, [Trailblazer], I wasn't being honest.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Tch, totally misjudged you. Guess I'll need to use a few extra fudgin' bullets on this guy.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: What did I expect with my awful summoning luck? I told you — a guy covered in gold is never good news.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Master, even as a joke, please don't say things that dishonor the knight's code.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Lyndon Skott! Well, *obscene language from the prison world era* me. How can there be an audience so uncultured!
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: You skipped all the best parts of the movie! This is the result of my entire life's work—
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: —And it was trash.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: You know nothing! I—I am the creator of the dream bubble movie genre. It was I who established the first film company in Penacony! If I hadn't given up on my monopoly on film-making technology, the Watchmaker and Maeven would never have achieved what they did!
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: So? Would that make the films you made... not bad?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: I'm even feeling a little bad for you now, Director Grady. You were thoroughly outclassed by true auteurs.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: As a master of marketing or an inventor, you're undoubtedly a success. But {RUBY_B#we}the audience{RUBY_E#} doesn't care what you gave in your efforts, they just know that your movie is terrible.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: *sigh* You can't feel the limits of {RUBY_B#our}the audience's{RUBY_E#} patience... It's just an endless, cliché-ridden, silent series of utterly unexciting gore. What a waste of everyone's time.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: It's no surprise that the audience eventually abandoned you.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Heh... Hahahahaha...
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Well, it's hopeless. This guy's probably gone mad.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Archer...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: What? I simply offered him a final shot. You're the one who drove him insane.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: What a sharp-tongued, amusing, and flamboyant actor you are! It's rare for anyone to make me go completely speechless during a debate...
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Didn't see that coming, did you?
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Strangling you all in this nightmare pantomime feels a bit dull now. Tell me, would you be interested in siding with Old Oti?
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: What are you yapping about this time? Tryin' to drive a wedge?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: If we join forces, we could sweep the rest of these opponents off the board in an instant. Surely, a senior executive of the Strategic Investment Department who understands investments better than anyone would make the right choice. Wouldn't you agree, Mr. Aventurine?
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: You seem particularly obsessed with me, Director. Is it because I, as an amateur film critic, repeatedly tore apart your masterpiece?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Of course it's because you're the cleverest one here, most aware of the fact that despite your apparent power, none of you have actually escaped my Bounded Field.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: For someone like you, betrayal is always an option to consider, not a moral absolute.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Someone like me? ...Hmph, you may be a terrible filmmaker, but you're not bad at reading people.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Fork me, you're not seriously—
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: A good businessman always evaluates the situation and adjusts their stance for better investment. I'm tired of this endless farce. Eliminating this many competitors at once is quite profitable.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Great! I love flexible actors like you. Now let me show my goodwill — let's move to the next scene. Your caliber deserves a much bigger stage.
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Archer. As my Servant, you'll come with me, right?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Taking orders from a hack like Grady? Seriously?
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Makes sense — compared to this lot, you and Grady are clearly cut from the same money-grubbing cloth.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: What's wrong with being a little underhanded if we can win?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: No, it should be my sword that delivers the final blow to the enemy commander.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Master, if you're just joking, I can still cover for you if you apologize now. But if you're serious, this won't end without blood being spilled.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: I'll ask one more time. Shall I remove your legs first? Or should I start by cutting off that irritating hand of yours, Mis-ter-A-ven-tur-ine?
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: So you still refuse... I should use my Command Spells to force you into submission, but I hate brands on the flesh that bend someone to another's will.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: If staying with them is your wish, then so be it. But sometimes... a change in perspective will make you see the gamble in its entirety.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: *sighs* That's right, killing you would erase my existence.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Well then, sorry everyone — I surrender, I give up.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: ARCHER!?
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: But as your Servant, I'll follow your commands.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Wait! Director, I can be a traitor too! I want more scenes too! Dir—
rows.speaker: Skott

rows.text: Fantastic! Two more exceptional leads at once! I'll give you bigger roles! Turn you into unstoppable monsters who tear everyone apart!
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: Step into the spotlight, Mr. Aventurine, and enjoy this special featurette I've crafted just for you!
rows.speaker: Director's Cut OST

rows.text: It's finally over...
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Is this Grand Theater ever gonna see a day of peace...? I'm starting to feel bad for the Bloodhounds and the Dreamweavers.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: No need to feel bad for a heritage building insured with hundreds of different policies. Old Oti would never allow himself to lose a single coin over that.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: So he dragged everyone into this Holy Grail War while hiding in the shadows, and none of you are gonna make him pay for it?
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Unfortunately, no Master was harmed in the making of this show. Even if we tried to hold him accountable, he'd probably just brush it off with his usual tricks — the best legal team money can buy and sky-high compensation.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: And... I fear the Holy Grail War has already given him returns far beyond what he's put into it.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: The silver lining is that this little spectacle will serve as the perfect excuse during negotiations for Madam Jade to pry open an even bigger opportunity in Penacony.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Does Skott have no rights?
Do Servants have no rights?
Tch, so the IPC is still the final winner of it all.
Mr. Skott's issues will be handled by the IPC.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Unfortunately, we are indeed not protected by human law.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Don't say it like that. This is a good thing for Penacony's shareholders.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Hmph. These Penaconian rules stinkin' of money won't keep me down. Lancer, let's go take care of that old fudger.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: I'm thinking you'll probably say "no." Owww, come on, {M#bro!}{F#sis!} You might not be curious, but the audience is still on the edge of their seats!
rows.speaker: Message from Mr. Cold Feet

rows.text: I knew it, {M#bro}{F#sis}! You're still thinking about old Sampo. And, I won't lie, the audience is waiting for it too.
rows.speaker: Message from Mr. Cold Feet

rows.text: Master, while I'm all in on that suggestion, time's running out. Without the Holy Grail holding us up, us Servants need to go back to where we belong.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Such a shame, brother... If we ever cross paths again, I'll take you to the finest honky-tonk in the cosmos for a drink.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Finest in the cosmos, huh? That's something to look forward to. Alright, no need for a tearful farewell for us bros, let's not ruin the good run we've had together. Till we meet again, buddy.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: And you two... Seriously, why can I never get a proper fight with you?
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: Is that so? I distinctly remember beating you.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: We should give him a good thrashing!
You know me, just a humble archer. Let's call this one another loss on me.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Tch, I'm done arguing with you lot. I'm gonna take another peek at Penacony's views before leaving for good.
rows.speaker: Lancer

rows.text: And so, it's time to say goodbye. Master, I have to admit that your fashion sense could use a little work, but... as a Servant, I'm genuinely glad to have fought by your side in this Holy Grail War.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: I can still see the determined heart of the child you once were underneath all your grand speeches and extravagant flair. You know, it would feel pretty good to be a hero of justice once in a while.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Ahem, let's skip the last-minute psychoanalysis, alright? And when it comes to fashion... You're not much better than me, "Guardian of Humanity."
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: That brings up a good point. Why would I, a "Guardian of Humanity," get summoned to a world without the Counter Force?
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: Are you leaving already?
Archer, you should know why you were summoned here.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: You were summoned as a Heroic Spirit.
A hero, huh? ...I'll chalk it up as a beautiful dream.
rows.speaker: Archer

rows.text: I saw your fears in your dream... but Master, don't be burdened by the emotions that come with being human: the fear of the unknown, the dread of loss, or the regret of what you couldn't achieve.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: If my existence can occasionally light the way forward for you... that would be more than I could hope for.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: Master, please send my regards to the person you will become in the future.
rows.speaker: Saber

rows.text: The Holy Grail... broke. What a shame.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: People have pursued it, fought for it, made sacrifices for it, and died for it, much like they did for our own Penacony.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: They poured their dreams into Penacony to shape the planet into what it is today. But the question is... has Penacony ever answered their dreams?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Look at this Memoria Singularity. Ten Amber Eras have passed, and out of those who once came here to build Penacony from the ground up, only one despicable old man is left. His friends, his enemies... they're all gone.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: A faint smile tugged at the man's cold face, before he vanished from sight. Soon, only the final pair of Master and Servant remained.

I must confess to both of you, my wish has been granted. No matter how you see me, no matter how deeply we hated each other in the past, the Holy Grail has recognized your achievements and brought you forth as Heroic Spirits...
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Don't you think this is a rather unique reunion of old friends? It's unfortunate that Mikhail, that old rascal, couldn't be here to join us.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Mr. Oti, your wish truly moves me.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: If I didn't know you better, I'd almost be swayed by your sweet words. A reunion of old friends? No. It's just another part of your business deal.
rows.speaker: Grady

rows.text: Grady, or perhaps I should now address you as Mr. Reca, is the editing of the footage complete? ...That is such an important task, after all.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: I've cut out everything related to the participants' privacy and kept only the most thrilling parts of the Holy Grail War. It may not be an artistic masterpiece, but it should meet your commercial expectations.
rows.speaker: Mr. Reca (?)

rows.text: That'd be enough for me. You artists always aim to carve your names into art's annals no matter the cost... Too bad those who actually succeed are as rare as the winners of the Holy Grail War.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: I'm not like that. What else can truly measure the effort you've put in apart from cold hard cash?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: ...The memories of former Heroic Spirits are also worthy compensation.
rows.speaker: Mr. Reca (?)

rows.text: Memories of a flop director like Grady? Do enlighten me, what worth do those hold?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: His memories are indeed positively worthless as a filmmaker, but when it comes to him as a person... those memories are treasures beyond compare.
rows.speaker: Mr. Reca (?)

rows.text: He has had his struggles, disappointments, and defiance... only to be reduced to another nameless nobody. That man is a symbol of the Penacony of his times, a most ridiculous clown... And a most genuine hero.
rows.speaker: Mr. Reca (?)

rows.text: How could I ever miss out on a memory with as many facets as a veritable diamond?
rows.speaker: Mr. Reca (?)

rows.text: But now I'm more curious about you, sir. You've spent so much money, only to create such an unsightly mess. Aren't you worried you'll end up in disgrace like Grady?
rows.speaker: Mr. Reca (?)

rows.text: A merchant at my age who still cares about dignity would be an absolute failure.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: In that case, my business here is settled. I'll take my leave.
rows.speaker: Mr. Reca (?)

rows.text: Alright. It's your turn, Miss Asna. I'll sign the declaration to renounce the trademark on your name and all rights to your creative works... Are you happy with that?
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: Happy? Never. But if you don't carry it through, I'll squeeze your puny neck with every ounce of my strength until I disappear... I'll watch you take your last breath, even if I know it won't actually kill you!
rows.speaker: Asna

rows.text: Goodbye, Penacony's most successful merchant. There's something I've always wanted to say to you —
rows.speaker: Asna

rows.text: I wish you were already dead.
rows.speaker: Asna

rows.text: Hahaha! Now that's a heartfelt confession! Asna, I do hope your wish comes true one day.
rows.speaker: Old Oti

rows.text: ...March 7th is always bringing back bizarre and curious things. One time, she even brought back something called a "Rating Pistol," and it only gave Pom-Pom a single point!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Also, watch out for Himeko's coffee. It's the most terrifying beverage Pom-Pom's ever encountered — but please don't ever tell her that to her face.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Is it worse than the tea from Granholm's hometown?
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: A hundred times worse!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: At the same time, aboard the Express.
Gather your thoughts to the present. If there really is a chance to fulfill a wish, what would yours be, [Trailblazer]?
Pfft, hahaha. I'd love to have a try!
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: And! And! [Trailblazer] is always dragging March 7th into trouble. Pom-Pom had such high hopes for Dan Heng, but even he's started to follow along now.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Mm-hmm.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: You passengers are all the same — Mikhail, you're spacing out again. What's going through that head of yours?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: That old fox didn't lose a thing.
Conductor, looks like it's time to say our goodbyes again.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Will you... be returning to the Express?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Maybe... I'm just happy to hear that so many people like me have boarded the Express over the years.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Too crude? No no no. Crude's good!

Hey {M#brother.}{F#sister.} Since you all looked pretty busy, I've headed out with Hook. Big thanks to Mr. Oti for buying this rare trinket I got my hands on. That's how I could afford this spontaneous trip.
rows.speaker: Message from Mr. Cold Feet

rows.text: The Nameless come and go. Some find a place they want to stay while others keep moving forward, just like the silver rails that never stop... That's the Astral Express. I'm sure the conductor's future will never be lonely.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: No.
I'm indeed curious.
The Holy Grail War is coming to an end, and wandering souls must return to their rest. I... need to go back to Penacony.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Far from the heat of battle, a Servant summoned under the Rider class stays on the sidelines. From the very beginning, it seems he had no intention of fighting.
As a Rider, he once built an unsinkable little ship named The Compass. As a Rider, he was once a Nameless who rode the stars aboard an interstellar Express.
Centuries have passed. Now, as a Heroic Spirit, the young man finally returns to the place where he once worked tirelessly. An old friend awaits him here.
Mikhail, remember: whether you leave or stay, the Astral Express will always be the home of the Nameless. Pom-Pom will always be here... waiting for your return!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: It's a deal then, Conductor. The next time the Express stops at Penacony... please sound the horn for me, Razalina, and Tiernan. If we can hear it... then we'll definitely come visit you.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: It's a promise!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Make a silent wish.
You see, wishes lose their power once spoken aloud.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: That does sound like something you'd say.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Anyway, the first Holy Grail War orchestrated by Old Oti ended up being the last one.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: But the dream bubble movie co-produced by Mr. Reca and Dr. Edward became a huge hit. Not only did it fill up movie theaters in Epsilon, it even created a new dream-chasing trend throughout the stars. Mr. Oti and the IPC's Penacony branch made quite the fortune from it.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: As Mr. Aventurine guessed, Oti simply brushed everything off as "entertainment" when questioned about placing Family heads and shareholders in danger.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: While compensation and lawsuits are inevitable, I suspect he already knew exactly what was coming even before the Holy Grail was activated.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Now, Old Oti did say he planned to give you some money, but even he thought that was too crude.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: So instead, he gave us the most valuable thing from this Holy Grail War.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Hmm? There's something inside the Holy Grail — I think this is a note for you, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: By the way, aren't you curious what old Sampo's wish to the Holy Grail was?
rows.speaker: Message from Mr. Cold Feet

rows.text: Alright, folks! The show's over! But if there's anything still out there that can hear and fulfill my wish —
rows.speaker: Message from Mr. Cold Feet

rows.text: "I wish for everyone in the world to be happy, joyful, free, and have their every desire fulfilled."
rows.speaker: Message from Mr. Cold Feet

rows.text: Make him pay for our emotional damage!
I'm not great at farewells...
Anything else you want to say to me?
Like you did?
Who's Heracles...
He's far too shrewd.
What about my appearance fee?
So THIS is his apology?
That old fox, always managing to get the most out of everything.
